He, exalted is He, informs of the deception of the polytheists regarding what they were in, and their excusing themselves from it by arguing with predestination (al-qadar), as a denial of the Messenger, may the blessings of Allah be upon him, and a slander against the message. Their saying is: ﴿Had Allah willed, we would not have worshipped anything besides Him—neither we nor our fathers—nor would we have prohibited anything without Him,﴾ meaning: the baheera, the sa'iba, the wasila and other things they had invented and devised from their own inclinations, for which Allah had sent down no authority. Then He, exalted is He, informed of their resemblance to those who preceded them, by His saying: ﴿Likewise did those before them act,﴾ meaning: in associating others with Allah and prohibiting, adhering to a similar doubt.

Ibn Kathir said: The substance of their speech is that if Allah, exalted is He, were averse to what we did, He would have denounced it against us with punishment, and would not have empowered us to do it. Allah, exalted is He, replied to their doubts: ﴿So is there upon the messengers except clear conveyance?﴾ meaning: the matter is not as you claim, that He did not denounce it to you. Rather, He denounced it to you in the strongest terms, forbade it to you with the most emphatic prohibition, and sent into every nation—meaning, into every generation and group of people—a messenger. All of them called to the worship of Allah and forbade the worship of anything other than Him: ﴿Worship Allah and avoid the Taghut﴾ [An-Nahl: 36], which is whatever is worshipped besides Him, glorified is He. Thus He, exalted is He, continued to send messengers to the people with this, from the time shirk arose among the children of Adam, from the era of Noah, the first messenger to the people of the earth, until the time of the Seal of the Prophets, may the blessings of Allah be upon him and upon them all. The call of all of them is one, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him that there is no deity except Me, so worship Me﴾ [Al-Anbiya: 25], and as He informed here in this verse. So how can any of the polytheists after this say: ﴿Had Allah willed, we would not have worshipped anything besides Him﴾?

His legislative will (al-mashi'a al-shar'iyya) regarding them is thus negated, because He forbade them from that through the tongues of His messengers. As for His existential will (al-mashi'a al-kawniyya), which is His enabling them to do so by decree, they have no proof in it—meaning, because it is among the secret of predestination which is forbidden to delve into. Then He, exalted is He, informed that He denounced them with punishment in this world, after the warning of the messengers, by His saying: ﴿Among them were those whom Allah guided﴾ [An-Nahl: 36], and the verse.

We have previously cited in Surah al-An'am what the scholars said concerning verses like this one. We shall also here cite what I read of Imam Ibn Taymiyya, may Allah have mercy on him, at the beginning of the second part of (Minhaj al-Sunna) concerning the verse, although a quotation from him has already preceded us. The verse is among the battlegrounds of understanding, so there is no harm in our clearing from its doubts the rust of misconceptions. He, may Allah have mercy on him, said: This is a station in which souls much plunge. For many people, when they are commanded to do what is obligatory upon them, make excuses by predestination and say: "Until Allah decrees that," or "Until Allah empowers me to that," or "Until Allah decides that." Likewise, when they are forbidden from doing what Allah has prohibited, they say: "Allah decreed it upon me," and similar speech. Arguing by predestination is a false and refuted argument, by the agreement of every person of intellect and religion among all the worlds. One who argues with it does not accept such an argument from others when they use it to justify an injustice they commit against him and a neglect of the rights they owe him. Rather, he demands from them what is due to him and punishes them for their aggression against him. It is of the same kind as the doubts of the sophists which arise in the sciences; you know their corruption by necessity, though they often occur to many people, to the point that one may doubt his own existence and other self-evident matters. Likewise, this (doubt) occurs in actions, until one thinks it is a doubt against the establishment of truthfulness and obligatory justice, and so on, and the permissibility of lying and injustice, and so on. But the hearts know by necessity that this is a false doubt. For this reason, no one accepts it upon careful examination, and no one argues with it except when he lacks knowledge of the proof concerning what he has done. When he knows that what he has done is the good, is what he was commanded, and is what ought to be done, he does not argue by predestination. Likewise, when he knows that what he did not do is not obligatory upon him, or is not beneficial, or is not what he was commanded, he does not argue by predestination. Rather, when he follows his desire without knowledge, he argues by predestination. For this reason, when the polytheists said: ﴿Had Allah willed, we would not have associated anything with Him, nor would our fathers, nor would we have prohibited anything﴾ [Al-An'am: 148], Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Do you have any knowledge that you could produce for us? You follow nothing but assumption, and you are only guessing﴾ [Al-An'am: 148], ﴿Say: "To Allah belongs the conclusive argument. So had He willed, He would have guided you all"﴾ [Al-An'am: 149]. These polytheists know by their natural disposition and their intellects that this argument is refuted and false. For if one of them wronged another, or took his property, or violated his wife, or killed his child, or persisted in injustice, and people forbade him from that, and he said: "Had Allah willed, I would not have done this," they would not accept this argument from him, nor would he accept it from others. One only argues with it to repel blame without any basis. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Do you have any knowledge that you could produce for us?﴾ [Al-An'am: 148], meaning that this shirk and prohibition are from the command of Allah, and that it is a benefit that ought to be done. ﴿You follow nothing but assumption﴾ [Al-An'am: 148], for you have no knowledge of that; you only assume it as a mere assumption. ﴿And you are only guessing﴾ [Al-An'am: 148], and fabricating. Your reliance in reality is your assumption and your guessing; your reliance in reality is not that Allah willed that and decreed it. For mere will and predestination are not a basis for anyone in an action, nor a proof of one person against another, nor an excuse for anyone, since all people share in predestination. If this were a proof and a basis, there would be no distinction between the just and the unjust, the truthful and the liar, the knowing and the ignorant, the righteous and the wicked. And there would be no difference between what benefits people among actions and what corrupts them, what benefits them and what harms them. These polytheists who argue by predestination to abandon what Allah sent His messengers with of His Oneness and faith in Him; if one of them argued with it against another regarding the forfeiture of his rights or the violation of his command, the other would not accept it from him. Rather, these polytheists would blame one another, be hostile to one another, and fight one another over the deed of one who intended to abandon their rights or to wrong them. So when the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came to them calling them to the right of Allah over His servants and obedience to His command, they argued by predestination; so they came to argue by predestination to abandon the right of their Lord and to violate His command, with what they would not accept from one who abandoned their right and violated their command. In the two Sahihs, from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: "O Mu'adh ibn Jabal! Do you know what the right of Allah over His servants is?" He said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "Its right over His servants is that they worship Him and not associate anything with Him. Do you know what the right of the servants over Allah is, if they do that?" He said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "Its right over them is that He not punish them."

The argument from divine decree (*qadar*) is the attitude of the people of *jahiliyyah* (pre-Islamic ignorance), who have no knowledge of what they do or leave undone: ﴿They follow nothing but conjecture, and they are only guessing﴾. They invoke it only to abandon the right of their Lord and to oppose His command, not to abandon what they themselves consider right or to oppose their own commands. For this reason you find that those who invoke and rely on it, from among the ascetics, the Sufis, the poor, the common people, the soldiers, the jurists and others, take refuge in it whenever they follow conjecture and what the souls desire. If they had knowledge and guidance, they would not argue from decree at all. Rather, they rely on it because of the absence of guidance and knowledge. This is a noble principle: whoever attends to it will know the source of error and misguidance for many people.

For this reason you find that the shaykhs and righteous people who uphold the commanding of good and forbidding of evil often enjoin their followers to acquire knowledge of the Law (*shar'*). Often, desires for certain things and love for them arise in them, and they follow their whims in these matters, thinking that it is the religion of God, the Exalted. Yet they have nothing beyond conjecture, taste (*dhawq*) and emotional feeling (*wijdan*), which return to the love of the self and its desire. So they sometimes argue from decree and sometimes from conjecture and guessing, while in reality they are following their whims. But when they follow knowledge, which is what the Lawgiver (*al-Shari'*) ﷺ brought, they depart from conjecture and what the souls desire, and they follow what has come to them from their Lord, which is guidance, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿So whoever follows My guidance, he will not go astray nor will he suffer﴾ [Ta-Ha: 123]. God, the Exalted, has mentioned this meaning about the polytheists in the surahs of al-An'am, al-Nahl and al-Zukhruf, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And they say, "If the Most Merciful had willed, we would not have worshipped them." They have no knowledge of that; they are only guessing﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 20]. Thus it is made clear that they have no knowledge of this; they are only guessing. And in the surah of al-An'am He said: ﴿Say, "Then to God belongs the conclusive proof"﴾ [al-An'am: 149], meaning the sending of messengers and the sending down of books, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿So that people will have no argument against God after the messengers﴾ [al-Nisa': 165]. Then He affirmed the decree by His saying: ﴿Had He willed, He would have guided you all﴾ [al-An'am: 149]. Thus He established the legal proof (*hujjah shar'iyyah*) and clarified the decreed will (*mashi'ah qadariyyah*), and both are true. And in al-Nahl He said: ﴿Those who associated said, "Had God willed, we would not have worshipped anything besides Him, neither we nor our fathers, nor would we have prohibited anything besides Him." Likewise did those before them do. So is there upon the messengers except clear notification?﴾ [al-Nahl: 35]. So He, glory be to Him and exalted, made clear that this statement is a denial of the messengers in what they brought, and is not a proof for them. For if it were a proof, it would be invoked to deny every truth and to justify every wrong. Thus in the natural disposition (*fitrah*) of the children of Adam, it is not a valid proof. Rather, whoever argues by it argues for the absence of knowledge and for following conjecture, like the deeds of those who denied the messengers with this objection. The conclusive proof belongs to God through the sending of messengers and the sending down of books, as is established in the authentic hadith from the Prophet ﷺ who said: "No one loves excuse more than God; for this reason He sent messengers as bearers of good news and warners. And no one loves praise more than God; for this reason He praised Himself. And no one is more jealous than God; for this reason He forbade indecencies, whether apparent or hidden."

He made clear that He, glory be to Him, loves praise, and loves to excuse, and hates indecencies. So He loves to be praised for justice and benevolence, and that He not be described as unjust. It is known that whoever lays down for his followers, saying, "Do this and do not do that," and makes this clear to them and removes their excuse, and then they transgress his limits and corrupt their affairs, he has the right to punish them and take vengeance upon them. If they then say, "Did not God decree this upon us? Had God willed, we would not have done this," it is said to them: You have no proof, and you have nothing with which to offer an excuse, and it is clear that what you did was either good or that you were excused in it. Therefore this speech is not acceptable from you.

[p. 3806] The proof has been established against you by what has preceded of clarification and warning. Suppose a ruler (*wali al-amr*) gave a group of people money to deliver to a town, and they traveled with it and left it in the desert where no one was present, and they spent the night far from it. Meanwhile the ruler had sent soldiers to fight some of the enemies, and those soldiers passed along that road, saw that money, and assumed it was a lost find (*luqatah*) that had no owner, so they took it and went away. Then it would be proper for him to punish the first group for their negligence and their failure to guard what he had commanded them to guard. And if they said to him, "You did not inform us that you would send soldiers after us, so that the money could be protected from them!" he would say: This is not obligatory upon me, and had I done it, it would have been an additional favor to you. But it was incumbent upon you to protect it as you protect deposits and trusts. His proof against them remains standing, and he would not be described as an oppressor among them, even if he did not help them by informing them of those soldiers. Rather, he performed what was beneficial in sending both the first and the latter.

God, glory be to Him and exalted, and to Him belongs the highest likeness, is a just Judge in all that He has made, and nothing goes outside His will and power. So when He commands people to guard the limits and to establish the obligations for their benefit, that is from His kindness toward them and making known to them what benefits them. And when He creates other matters, and then they are negligent and transgress because of His creating those other matters, He is just and wise in creating this and creating that, and in commanding this and commanding that. And even if He did not supply the first group with an increase by which they would guard themselves against negligence and aggression, especially with His knowledge that such an increase, had He created it, would have entailed the loss of a greater benefit, for opposites cannot be combined.

The purpose here is that no one argues from decree except as an argument of mere causal justification, to support following the truth that knowledge has made clear. For man is living, sensing, and moved by will. For this reason the Prophet ﷺ said: "The truest of names is al-Harith and Hammam." Al-Harith is the one who earns and works, and al-Hammam is the one who is moved by aspiration (*hamm*). Aspiration is the origin of will and intention. So every person is a *harith* and a *hammam*, one who is moved by will, and this does not occur except after sensation and awareness. For will is preceded by awareness of the object willed, so there is no conceiving of will, love, longing, choice, or seeking except after awareness and what is of its kind, such as sensation, knowledge, hearing, sight, smell, taste, touch, and similar things. This perception and awareness is the prerequisite of will, love and seeking. The living being is naturally disposed to love what benefits it and suits it, and to hate what harms it and repels it. When it conceives of the thing that suits it and benefits it, it wills and loves it. And if it conceives of the thing that harms it, it hates it and recoils from it. But that conception may be knowledge, or it may be conjecture and guessing. If he knows that what he wills is beneficial, that it is the good and what suits him, then he is upon guidance and truth. And if he has no knowledge of that, he is following conjecture and what his soul desires. But if knowledge and clarification come to him that this is not a benefit, he begins to argue from decree, an argument of obstinacy and evasion, not an argument of reliance upon truth and knowledge. Thus no one argues from decree, inwardly or outwardly, except for lack of knowledge of what the truth is. And if this is the case, whoever argues from decree against the messengers is acknowledging that he does not have knowledge of what he holds, and that he speaks without knowledge. Whoever speaks without knowledge is false in his speech, and whoever argues without knowledge has a refuted argument. Either he is ignorant, in which case he must follow knowledge; or he has come to know the truth and followed his whim, in which case he must follow the truth and abandon his whim. It is thus made clear that the one who argues from decree is following his whim without knowledge: ﴿And who is more astray than one who follows his whim without guidance from God?﴾ [al-Qasas: 50]. End of quotation. He has a comprehensive continuation that is worth consulting.

Al-Qashani said regarding this verse: They only said that out of obstinacy and stubbornness, from excessive ignorance, and as a challenge to the monotheists, based on their own doctrine. For if they had said it out of knowledge and certainty, they would have been monotheists, not polytheists, by ascribing will and influence to other than God. For whoever knows that nothing can occur without the will of God, knows that if every being in the world willed something, and God did not will it, it could not occur. So he acknowledges the negation of power and will from all besides God, and thus he would not remain a polytheist. God, the Exalted, said: ﴿Had God willed, they would not have associated﴾ [al-An'am: 107]. And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So did those before them﴾, i.e., in denying the messengers out of obstinacy. End of quotation.

The Imam, the Mufti of Egypt, said in his tafsir of Surat al-Asr, from this discussion, the following in substance: Reason, the Law, the senses and inner feeling (*wijdan*) all agree that the act of the servant is his act. That all things return to God, the Exalted, and the existence of contingent beings, is merely their attribution to Him. It is not conceivable to consider them existing except when they are considered as dependent upon Him, which is established by proof, and indeed nearly reaches self-evidence in this way. The same is said regarding the greatness of God's power, the Exalted. If He wills, He can strip us of the power and choice that He has granted us. This is a matter we witness every day: we arrange something, then obstacles come to prevent its realization that were not in our reckoning, and we undertake a work, then our power is cut off from completing it. All of this is beyond dispute. The comprehensiveness of God's knowledge of what has been and what will be is established by proof, and there is no doubt about it among the adherents of the religion. Therefore it is obligatory upon the Muslim to believe that God is the Creator of everything in the manner that He knows, and to affirm the attribution of his action to Him as is self-evident to him. He knows what He has commanded him and avoids what He has forbidden him by using that choice which he finds within himself. He is not obliged after this to raise his gaze beyond it. God has censured the polytheists for their saying: ﴿Had God willed, we would not have associated, neither we nor our fathers, nor would we have prohibited anything﴾ [al-An'am: 148]. Traditions have come with meanings in mutual reinforcement (*mutawatir al-ma'na*) forbidding delving into the decree and its secret. If the servant patiently persevered to the utmost patience, he would stop at what God has set for him as limit, and would not incline by himself to transgress the limits of God that He has set for His servants. I do not wish to speak on this question more than this; otherwise I would have left the patient, and plunged into the question of decree with those who plunge. Whoever is seized by confusion and imagines that we must believe the servant has no act, has contradicted the Book of God and disobeyed the Messenger of God. And I may say, and my reliance is upon God in what I say: whoever says that goes outside the religion of God and nullifies the Law of God, so let the believer in God beware of saying that. End of quotation.

In another place he said: Arguing for abandoning action on the basis of decree is among the doctrines of the atheists. The Noble Book has come to denounce their belief and to censure them for it. It has related to us what they used to say, such as: ﴿Had God willed, we would not have associated, neither we nor our fathers, nor would we have prohibited anything﴾ [al-An'am: 148]. It is not permissible for any of us, while claiming to believe in the Qur'an, to argue with what the polytheists used to argue with. End of quotation. And His, the Exalted, saying:

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, Exalted is He:

[-1] ﴿If you are eager for their guidance, indeed Allah does not guide those He leads astray, and they will have no helpers.﴾ ﴿And they swore by Allah with their most emphatic oaths that Allah will not resurrect those who die. Yes [He will], as a promise binding upon Him, but most of the people do not know.﴾ [An-Nahl: 38].

﴿If you are eager for their guidance, indeed Allah does not guide those He leads astray﴾ — i.e., those in whom He creates misguidance due to their own evil choice. ﴿And they will have no helpers﴾ — i.e., no one who will help them toward guidance, or who will ward off the punishment from them.

Then Exalted is He explained another kind of their falsehoods, which is their denial of resurrection, by His words:

﴿And they swore by Allah with their most emphatic oaths﴾ [An-Nahl: 38] — i.e., exerting themselves in them. Here {jahd} (جَهْدَ, "utmost effort") is a verbal noun in the position of a circumstantial accusative (ḥāl): ﴿Allah will not resurrect those who die. Yes [He will], as a promise binding upon Him, but most of the people do not know﴾ [An-Nahl: 38] — i.e., that He will resurrect them, yet they pronounce definitively its non-occurrence! And that it is a promise (wa'dan) binding upon Him, yet they deny it. This is due to their ignorance of the affairs of Allah, mighty is His majesty, concerning knowledge, power, wisdom and other attributes of perfection, and concerning what is permissible for Him and what is not, and their failure to comprehend the secret of creation and its ultimate purpose, and that resurrection is among what wisdom requires. This was conveyed by Abu al-Su'ud.

Then He mentioned His wisdom regarding the Return and the gathering of bodies on the Day of Mutual Calling, by His words, glorified is He:

(p-3810)

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, the Exalted:

[39-40] "That He may make clear to them that about which they differ, and that those who disbelieved may know that they were liars" and "Indeed, Our word to a thing when We intend it is only that We say to it, 'Be,' and it is." [An-Nahl: 40].

"That He may make clear to them that about which they differ" – which is the truth – "and that those who disbelieved may know that they were liars" – and that they had been upon misguidance before it. "That those who disbelieved may know that they were liars," i.e., in their falsehoods, especially in their belief in the denial of resurrection. Therefore the angels of punishment will say to them on the Day of Resurrection: "This is the Fire which you used to deny" [At-Tur: 14]. Then He explained His great power, and that nothing whatsoever can overcome Him, by His saying, glorified is He:

"Indeed, Our word to a thing when We intend it is only that We say to it, 'Be,' and it is" [An-Nahl: 40], i.e., it comes into existence as He wills its bringing into being, like His saying, the Exalted: "And Our command is but one, like a glance of the eye" [Al-Qamar: 50], and His saying: "Your creation and your resurrection are not but as a single soul" [Luqman: 28].

Az-Zamakhshari said: "Qawluna" (Our word) is the subject (mubtada'), "an naqula" (that We say) is its predicate (khabar), and "kun fa-yakun" (Be, and it is) is from "kana" (to be) in its complete usage (al-tammah), which means coming into being and existence. That is: when We intend the existence of a thing, there is nothing but that We say to it, "Come into being," and it comes into being immediately after that, without delay. This is an illustration, because what He wills cannot be resisted by Him, and its existence at the time of His will, the Exalted, is without any delay, like the existence of the thing commanded at the command of an obeyed commander when it reaches the obedient, compliant subordinate, and there is no saying there. The meaning is: the bringing into being of every thing that is within God's power, the Exalted, is with this ease. So how could resurrection, which is among the things that are within the scope of what is possible, be impossible for Him? End of quote.

Al-Shihab said: Thus what was said is refuted: that "kun" (Be), if it is an address to the non-existent, is impossible; and if it is an address to the existent, it would be bringing into existence what already exists. There is a subtle discussion of this verse in Surat al-Baqarah, so refer back to it.

Then God, the Exalted, informed about His recompense for the emigrants (muhajirun) who left the abode, the family and the close friends, seeking His reward and desiring His good pleasure, by His saying:

Then God, the Exalted, informed about His recompense for the emigrants (muhajirun) who left the abode, the family and the close friends, seeking His reward and desiring His good pleasure, by His saying:

(p-3811)

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 16, verse 41:

On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[41] ﴿And those who emigrated for the sake of Allah after they had been wronged – We will surely settle them in this world in a good place. And the reward of the Hereafter is greater, if only they knew.﴾

﴿Those who emigrated for the sake of Allah﴾: that is, sincerely seeking His countenance, or for His cause. They are either the emigrants to Abyssinia (al-Habasha), whose people in Mecca intensified their harm to them until they left among them for the lands of the Abyssinians by his command ﷺ, out of fear of trial and in flight to Allah the Exalted with their religion. They were eighty-three men, besides their young children, and this was the first emigration in Islam. The fact that the surah is Meccan supports this.

Or they are the emigrants to Medina; he informed of it before its occurrence or after it, except that it was attached to the Meccan (surahs). His saying, exalted is He, ﴿after they had been wronged﴾: that is, they were harmed, and their trial from the religion was intended. ﴿We will surely settle them in this world in a good place﴾: meaning, by victory over those who wronged them, and by giving them their land and their homes. ﴿And the reward of the Hereafter is greater, if only they knew﴾: meaning, [the reward of the Hereafter is greater for] those who persecuted them and wronged them.

It is narrated that ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, whenever he gave an emigrant (al-muhajirin) his stipend, would say: "Take it, may Allah bless it for you. This is what Allah promised you in this world, and what He has stored up for you in the Hereafter is better." Then He, exalted is He, described them with His saying:

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[42-44] ﴿Those who have been patient and upon their Lord they rely.﴾ ﴿We sent not before you except men to whom We revealed, so ask the people of the reminder if you do not know.﴾ [al-Nahl: 43] ﴿With clear proofs and scriptures. And We have sent down to you the Reminder that you may make clear to the people what has been sent down to them, and that they may give thought.﴾ [al-Nahl: 44].

﴿Those who have been patient﴾ means: patient over what they were harmed for the sake of Allah. ﴿And upon their Lord they rely﴾ means: so they do not fear anyone other than Him. The two qualities mentioned, patience (sabr) and reliance (tawakkul), are among the principal attributes that the one who calls to the truth, and who defends it, must possess as part of his character, since no success in any goal is achieved except through them. When they marvelled at Allah's revelation to His Messenger and His choosing him for His message, it was said in refutation of their doubt:

﴿We sent not before you except men to whom We revealed, so ask the people of the reminder if you do not know.﴾ [al-Nahl: 43] It means: the People of the Book or the scholars of the rabbis, so that they may inform you that no angel from the inhabitants of heaven was sent for the general call. Here "the reminder" (al-dhikr) may mean the Book, because of what it contains of remembrance and admonition, as in His words: ﴿It is nothing but a reminder﴾ [Sad: 87], or it may mean the preservation of the reports of earlier nations. The verse indicates the obligation to refer to the scholars in matters one does not know. Some have cited it as evidence for the permissibility of taqlid (following a scholar's opinion) in the subsidiary rulings for the layman. On this there is a lengthy discussion in al-Fulani's "Iqaz al-Himam" (Awakening of Resolves), so refer to it if you wish. He touched on a portion of it in "Fath al-Bayan" (Opening of the Clarification).

His words, Exalted is He: ﴿With clear proofs and scriptures﴾ [al-Nahl: 44] mean: with the signs that demonstrate their truthfulness and the books that guide to the welfare of creation. The prepositional phrase is connected to an implied element indicated by what precedes it, i.e., "We sent them." Or it is connected to "We sent," or to "We revealed," or to "you do not know," with the conditional clause serving as rebuke and reproof. ﴿And We have sent down to you the Reminder﴾ [al-Nahl: 44] means: the Qur'an, which reminds and awakens from the slumber of heedlessness. ﴿That you may make clear to the people what has been sent down to them﴾ [al-Nahl: 44] means: of what they were commanded, forbidden, promised and warned. ﴿And that they may give thought﴾ [al-Nahl: 44] means: that they may look into their own selves and so be guided, and thereby succeed in salvation in both abodes; or that they may reflect on what it contains of lessons, and so guard against what befell the former peoples. For this reason he followed it with his words:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[45] ﴿Do those who devised evil schemes feel safe that Allah will cause the earth to swallow them, or that the punishment will come upon them from where they do not perceive?﴾

﴿Do those who devised evil schemes feel safe﴾ means: the intoxicating evil [schemes] (al-muskirat al-sayyi'at) that were recounted about them. Then (fa-hiya) it is either an adjective of an omitted verbal noun (masdar), or an object of "makarū" (devised), with the verb implicitly carrying the sense of "'amilū" (did, committed) (this is tadmin, implicit meaning): ﴿that Allah will cause the earth to swallow them, or that the punishment will come upon them from where they do not perceive﴾

That is: from a direction they do not know of, just as the one targeted by a schemer does not perceive the schemer's intent.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 16, verses 46–48:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[46–48] ﴿Or He seizes them in their going to and fro, and they cannot escape [it].﴾ ﴿Or He seizes them with gradual diminution. Indeed, your Lord is Kind and Merciful.﴾ [al-Nahl: 47] ﴿Have they not considered what things Allah has created, how their shadows turn from the right and the left, prostrating to Allah while they are humbled?﴾ [al-Nahl: 48].

﴿Or He seizes them in their going to and fro﴾, i.e., their striving in livelihoods and their occupation with them. ﴿And they cannot escape [it]﴾, i.e., they cannot overpower their Lord in any state they may be in.

﴿Or He seizes them with gradual diminution﴾ [al-Nahl: 47], i.e., with an expectation of destruction and a fear of it, for this is more forceful and more severe. Or [it means] We diminish their bodies, their wealth and their fruits until they perish. It is said: "takhawwafahu" means he diminished him and took from his extremities. ﴿Indeed, your Lord is Kind and Merciful﴾ [al-Nahl: 47], i.e., in that He forbears with you and does not hasten to punish you. Then Exalted is He informed of His greatness, majesty and magnificence through the submission of all His creatures, inanimate and animate, and the accountable among jinn, humankind and angels, to Him, Glorified is He, by His saying: ﴿Have they not considered what things Allah has created﴾ [al-Nahl: 48], i.e., any body that has a shadow, ﴿how their shadows turn﴾ [al-Nahl: 48], i.e., return little by little, ﴿from the right and the left﴾ [al-Nahl: 48], i.e., from both sides of each one of them, in the morning and in the evening, ﴿prostrating to Allah﴾ [al-Nahl: 48], i.e., submitting to Him according to His will in extension, contraction and other [states], not resisting Him in what He has subjected them to, ﴿while they are humbled﴾ [al-Nahl: 48], i.e., abased. In their plural form he gave precedence to the one who understands, so He used the particle wa (and). Or because humbling (dukhur) is one of the attributes of the rational. So it is either a case of predominance (taghlib) or a metaphor, and likewise the pronoun "hum" (they) as well, since it is specific to the rational, so it is permissible to regard what is mentioned in it and to make what follows it run in accordance with the mushakala (concordance of the statement).

(p-3814) A Subtle Point:

Ibn al-Sa'igh has a subtle explanation regarding the secret of the singular "yamin" (right) and the plural "shama'il" (left), and its summary is that he considered the end-point in both: the shadow of the morning diminishes until only a little of it remains, so it is as if it is in one direction. In the evening it is the reverse, because it spreads over all directions. Thus both end-states were taken into account. This is from the perspective of meaning.

As for the perspective of wording, it was pluralized to agree with "sujjadan" (prostrating) adjacent to it, just as the first was made singular because of the adjacency of the pronoun in "zilalahu" (its shadows), and the singular was given precedence because it is the more original and lighter form. And "ʿan al-yamin" (from the right) is connected to "yatafayya'u" (turn) or is a circumstantial clause (hal). Thus [it is stated] in al-'Inayah.

Then he explained the prostration of all other created beings, whether or not they have shadows, by His saying, exalted is He:

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[49] ﴿To Allah prostrates whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth of creatures, and the angels, and they are not arrogant.﴾

﴿To Allah prostrates whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth of creatures, and the angels, and they﴾ — i.e., the angels, despite their high rank — ﴿are not arrogant﴾, i.e., from worshipping Him and prostrating to Him.

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[50] ﴿They fear their Lord above them, and they do what they are commanded.﴾

﴿They fear their Lord above them, and they do what they are commanded.﴾ That is: [they perform] acts of obedience and [the] management [of affairs]. He (the author) cited His saying ﴿above them﴾ as evidence for the affirmation of "above-ness" (al-fawqiyyah) and "highness" (al-uluww) for Allah, exalted is He. The memorizer of hadith al-Dhahabi (al-Hafiz al-Dhahabi) composed a book on this subject titled (al-Uluww, "The Highness"), and Ibn al-Qayyim (Ibn al-Qayyim) composed (al-Juyush al-Islamiyyah, "The Islamic Armies"), among others. The wise scholar Ibn Rushd (al-Hakim Ibn Rushd) expounded on it at length in (Manahij al-Dawlah, "The Methods of the State"), so let him refer to it. All of them agree that it is highness without likening or comparing [Allah to anything]. The Salaf alone held to the danger of ta'wil (figurative interpretation) and ta'til (denial of attributes). And his saying:

On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[51] ﴿And Allah said: Do not take two gods. He is but one God; so fear Me alone.﴾

"And Allah said: Do not take two gods. He is but one God; so fear Me alone" is an announcement of His explicit prohibition of associating partners with Him, and of His command to worship Him alone. He specified this number (two) because it is the least number, so the negation of what is above it is known by implication (al-dalalah). If it is said: "one" and "two" are explicit in their meanings, and with them there is no need to mention a number, as a number is mentioned with plurals, as in "men, three" (rijal thalathah) and "mares, four" (afras arba'ah), because the counted noun is devoid of indication of a specific number; so why was the number mentioned with them? I answer: the number indicates two things, the category (al-jinsiyyah) and the specific number. When the second is intended, it is stated explicitly, to indicate that it is the purpose for which the speech was brought and to which the prohibition is directed, to the exclusion of anything else. For the singular may be intended to denote the category, as in: "How excellent a man is Zayd" (ni'ma al-rajul Zayd). Likewise the dual, as in his saying:

"Indeed fire is kindled by two sticks, and indeed war begins with words."

It has also been said: he mentioned the number to hint that duality contradicts divinity. It is thus in the meaning of His saying: ﴿Had there been in them gods other than Allah, they would have been ruined﴾ [al-Anbiya': 22]. Therefore he stated it explicitly, and it was followed by mention of oneness, which is among the necessary attributes of divinity.

Al-Shihab said: there is no need to make the pronoun refer to the truly worshipped Deity intended by the name Allah, by way of istikhdam.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And Allah said﴾ is conjoined to His saying: ﴿And to Allah prostrates﴾ [al-Nahl: 49], or to His saying: ﴿And We have sent down to you the Reminder﴾ [al-Nahl: 44]. It has also been said that it is conjoined to: ﴿what Allah has created﴾ [al-Nahl: 48], in the style of:

"I fed them straw and cold water"

That is: ﴿Have they not looked at what Allah has created?﴾ [al-Nahl: 48] and not heard what Allah has said? Its strain is not hidden. In His saying: ﴿so fear Me alone﴾ there is a shift (iltifat) from the third person to the first person, for emphasis in instilling awe. For frightening someone present, face to face, is more forceful than instilling awe in someone absent, especially after describing Him with oneness and divinity, which require majesty and complete power to exact retribution. And His saying, exalted is He:

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth, and to Him is obedience due, constantly. Then will you fear other than Allah?﴾ ﴿Whatever blessing you have is from Allah. Then when harm touches you, to Him you cry out for help.﴾ [An-Nahl: 53] ﴿Then when He removes harm from you, behold, a faction of you associates others with their Lord.﴾ [An-Nahl: 54] ﴿So that they deny what We have given them. So enjoy yourselves, for you will soon know.﴾ [An-Nahl: 55]

﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth﴾ is either *ma'tuf* (conjoined) to His words ﴿Indeed, He is but one God﴾ [An-Nahl: 51], or to the predicate, or it is *mustani'af* (resumptive, a new clause). ﴿And to Him is obedience due, constantly﴾ means: worship is binding upon Him alone. Its being binding upon Him is incompatible with fearing others, since it requires that He, exalted is He, be singled out for awe and dread. This is like His words: ﴿Do they seek other than the religion of Allah, while to Him submits whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly, and to Him they will be returned?﴾ [Al 'Imran: 83]

﴿Then will you fear other than Allah?﴾ means: while He is the master of benefit and harm. 50 ﴿Whatever blessing you have is from Allah﴾ [An-Nahl: 53], meaning it is from His bounty and kindness. ﴿Then when harm touches you, to Him you cry out for help﴾ [An-Nahl: 53], meaning you supplicate only to Him, because you know that none can remove it except Him, glorified is He. *Al-juwar* (the crying out) is raising the voice. It is said: جأر when he exceeds in supplication and entreaty. Its origin is the cry of wild animals.

﴿Then when He removes harm from you, behold, a faction of you associates others with their Lord﴾ [An-Nahl: 54], meaning: by attributing the blessing to other than Him and seeing it as coming from that other, and likewise by attributing harm to other than Him, placing the blame for it upon that other, and seeking relief from it through that other. This is ingratitude for blessings and heedlessness of the Benefactor, which are alluded to by His words:

﴿So that they deny what We have given them﴾ [An-Nahl: 55], meaning: of the blessing of His removing harm from them. The *lam* here is *lam al-'aqibah* (the lam of consequence and outcome): ﴿So enjoy yourselves, for you will soon know﴾ [An-Nahl: 55], meaning: the consequence of that disbelief. In this there is an indication of the severity of the threat, and that it is known only by direct witnessing and cannot be described; therefore it is left vague.

Al-Qashani has another interpretation. He said: "Or ﴿for you will soon know﴾, through the manifestation of monotheism, that there is no effect of anything other than Allah upon anything."

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth, and to Him is obedience due, constantly. Then will you fear other than Allah?﴾ ﴿Whatever blessing you have is from Allah. Then when harm touches you, to Him you cry out for help.﴾ [An-Nahl: 53] ﴿Then when He removes harm from you, behold, a faction of you associates others with their Lord.﴾ [An-Nahl: 54] ﴿So that they deny what We have given them. So enjoy yourselves, for you will soon know.﴾ [An-Nahl: 55]

﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth﴾ is either *ma'tuf* (conjoined) to His words ﴿Indeed, He is but one God﴾ [An-Nahl: 51], or to the predicate, or it is *mustani'af* (resumptive, a new clause). ﴿And to Him is obedience due, constantly﴾ means: worship is binding upon Him alone. Its being binding upon Him is incompatible with fearing others, since it requires that He, exalted is He, be singled out for awe and dread. This is like His words: ﴿Do they seek other than the religion of Allah, while to Him submits whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly, and to Him they will be returned?﴾ [Al 'Imran: 83]

﴿Then will you fear other than Allah?﴾ means: while He is the master of benefit and harm. 50 ﴿Whatever blessing you have is from Allah﴾ [An-Nahl: 53], meaning it is from His bounty and kindness. ﴿Then when harm touches you, to Him you cry out for help﴾ [An-Nahl: 53], meaning you supplicate only to Him, because you know that none can remove it except Him, glorified is He. *Al-juwar* (the crying out) is raising the voice. It is said: جأر when he exceeds in supplication and entreaty. Its origin is the cry of wild animals.

﴿Then when He removes harm from you, behold, a faction of you associates others with their Lord﴾ [An-Nahl: 54], meaning: by attributing the blessing to other than Him and seeing it as coming from that other, and likewise by attributing harm to other than Him, placing the blame for it upon that other, and seeking relief from it through that other. This is ingratitude for blessings and heedlessness of the Benefactor, which are alluded to by His words:

﴿So that they deny what We have given them﴾ [An-Nahl: 55], meaning: of the blessing of His removing harm from them. The *lam* here is *lam al-'aqibah* (the lam of consequence and outcome): ﴿So enjoy yourselves, for you will soon know﴾ [An-Nahl: 55], meaning: the consequence of that disbelief. In this there is an indication of the severity of the threat, and that it is known only by direct witnessing and cannot be described; therefore it is left vague.

Al-Qashani has another interpretation. He said: "Or ﴿for you will soon know﴾, through the manifestation of monotheism, that there is no effect of anything other than Allah upon anything."

Then He (Exalted) explained, through His saying, some of the defects of the polytheists:

The discussion of the interpretation (ta'wil) of His saying, exalted is He:

[56-57] ﴿And they assign to what they do not know a share of what We have provided for them. By Allah, you will surely be questioned about what you used to invent.﴾ ﴿And they assign to Allah daughters, exalted is He, while for themselves is what they desire.﴾

﴿And they assign to what they do not know﴾ means: to their gods, which have no knowledge, because they are inanimate. ﴿A share of what We have provided for them﴾ means: of the crops, the livestock, and other things, seeking nearness to them. ﴿By Allah, you will surely be questioned about what you used to invent﴾ means: concerning your claim that they are gods to whom one may draw near. A parallel to this verse has occurred in Surah al-An'am, in His saying: ﴿And they assign to Allah a share of what He has created of the crops and livestock﴾ [al-An'am: 136], and so its details should be consulted there.

﴿And they assign to Allah daughters, exalted is He, while for themselves is what they desire﴾ [al-Nahl: 57] This is an explanation of one of their great abominations, namely their making the angels, who are the servants of the Most Merciful, daughters of Allah. Thus they attributed to Him, exalted is He, a child, when He has no child. They dared to utter the like of this, and to attribute to Him the lesser of the two kinds of offspring, which is daughters, while they themselves would not be content with them for themselves, because they desire males, that is, they choose them for themselves and disdain daughters. He has declared His most holy station far above that by His saying: ﴿exalted is He﴾ [al-Nahl: 57], that is, above their falsehood and their statement. In this there is an expression of astonishment at their audacity in uttering this reprehensible word, and at their dividing with Him His majesty by claiming exclusivity for themselves, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Is for you the male and for Him the female? That, then, is an unjust division﴾ [al-Najm: 21-22]. And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Unquestionably, it is of their falsehood that they say: "Allah has begotten"; and indeed, they are liars﴾ [al-Saffat: 151-152]; ﴿He has chosen daughters over sons﴾ [al-Saffat: 153]; ﴿What is [wrong] with you? How do you judge?﴾ [al-Saffat: 154]. Then He alluded to the intensity of their aversion to females, by what represents the greatness of that attribution to the Most Sacred Presence and its atrocity, by His saying, exalted and high is He:

The discussion of the words of God Most High:

[58-59] ﴿When one of them is given the news of a female, his face becomes dark, and he is filled with suppressed rage.﴾ ﴿He hides himself from the people because of the evil of the news he has been given. Shall he keep it in humiliation, or bury it in the dust? Surely evil is what they judge.﴾ [al-Nahl: 59].

﴿When one of them is given the news of a female, his face becomes﴾, i.e., becomes or remains, all day long: ﴿dark﴾, i.e., changed by the grief, sorrow, anger and aversion that arise in him upon this news. The blackness and whiteness of the face express displeasure and delight, either as a metonymy (kinayah) or as a metaphor (majaz). ﴿And he is filled with suppressed rage﴾, i.e., intensely enraged at his wife, because, in his assumption, there has befallen him from her what necessitates the utmost shame. So much so that he ﴿hides himself from the people﴾ [al-Nahl: 59], i.e., he conceals himself from them, ﴿because of the evil of the news he has been given﴾ [al-Nahl: 59], i.e., on account of it and out of fear of reproach for it. Then he ponders what to do with it, which is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Shall he keep it in humiliation﴾ [al-Nahl: 59], i.e., speaking to himself and reflecting on whether to leave it in disgrace and abasement, not granting it an inheritance nor caring for it, preferring the male children over it. ﴿Or bury it in the dust﴾ [al-Nahl: 59], i.e., hide it and bury it alive in it. ﴿Surely evil is what they judge﴾ [al-Nahl: 59], i.e., how evil is their judgment, in that they make the child whose state is this one of lowliness and humiliation in their sight belong to God, Exalted and Sanctified be He, while they assign to themselves what is the opposite of this description. And His saying, Exalted is He:

And His saying, Exalted is He:

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 16, verse 60:

(p-3820) The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[60] ﴿For those who do not believe in the Hereafter is the evil description, and for Allah is the highest description. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.﴾

﴿For those who do not believe in the Hereafter﴾ i.e., like those whose evil qualities were mentioned: ﴿the evil description﴾ i.e., the attributes of abasement arising from need for offspring, the dislike of females and burying them alive out of fear of poverty, all of which is described by weakness, deficiency and extreme stinginess. He placed the relative pronoun in the position of the pronoun, to indicate that the basis of their being characterized by those vile traits is disbelief in the Hereafter. ﴿And for Allah is the highest description﴾ i.e., the attribute of lofty status, and He is the Self-Sufficient above the worlds, the absolute perfection, and the One exalted above the marks of created beings. ﴿And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.﴾

Then He, exalted is He, informed about His forbearance toward His creation despite their wrongdoing, by His saying:

The discussion of the Almighty's words:

﴿And if God were to seize mankind for their wrongdoing, He would not leave upon it [the earth] a single creature. But He defers them to a specified term. So when their term comes, they cannot delay it an hour, nor can they advance it.﴾ ﴿And they assign to God what they dislike, and their tongues describe the lie that theirs is the best [reward]. Without doubt, theirs is the Fire, and they will be neglected.﴾ [al-Nahl: 61–62]

﴿And if God were to seize mankind for their wrongdoing﴾, i.e., for their disbelief and their disobedience, including the evils already enumerated: ﴿He would not leave upon it﴾, i.e., upon the earth, which is indicated by "mankind" (al-nas), ﴿a single creature﴾. The phrase ﴿a single creature﴾ means that He would have destroyed them entirely, because of the evil of the wrongdoers: ﴿But He defers them to a specified term﴾ (p-3821), i.e., a determined time required by wisdom. Among them, whoever seeks forgiveness is forgiven, and whoever persists is increased in punishment. ﴿So when their term comes﴾, i.e., the specified term: ﴿they cannot delay it an hour, nor can they advance it.﴾

﴿And they assign to God﴾ [al-Nahl: 62], i.e., they attribute to Him: ﴿what they dislike﴾ [al-Nahl: 62], i.e., daughters and partners. They are disdainful of daughters, just as they dislike sharing their wealth with anyone. This is a repetition of what preceded, serving as a further rebuke and a preparation for His words:

﴿and their tongues describe the lie that theirs is the best [reward]﴾ [al-Nahl: 62], i.e., they assign that to God, while claiming that they will have the best outcome with God, if there is any return, as He related of them in His words: ﴿And if I am returned to my Lord, surely I will have the best [reward] with Him﴾ [Fussilat: 50]. That is, these people combined evil deeds with wishful thinking about the impossible, expecting to be rewarded with good for it.

It has been reported that when the Ka'bah was renovated, there was found written on one of its stones: "You do evil deeds and you are repaid with good deeds. Indeed, [it is so], just as grapes are gathered from thorns." And ﴿that theirs [is the best]﴾ [al-Nahl: 62] etc. is a substitute for "the lie" (al-kadhib), or it is taken as "that for them" (bi-anna lahum).

Al-Shihab said: His words, "﴿and their tongues describe the lie﴾" [al-Nahl: 62], are among the eloquent and innovative expressions of speech, like the saying: "Her eye describes magic," i.e., she is a sorceress; and "Her slender form describes slenderness," i.e., she is slender-waisted.

Abu al-'Ala al-Ma'arri said:

*The lightning of al-Ma'arrah passed after a lull, and then it spent the night at Barramah, describing weariness.*

(p-3822) Then He rejected their statement and affirmed its opposite with His words, glorified is He: ﴿Without doubt, theirs is the Fire, and they will be neglected﴾ [al-Nahl: 62], i.e., they will be hastened toward it and placed in front of it, from (al-faraṭ), meaning one who precedes to the watering place. It is said: "I sent him ahead (afratuhu) in seeking water" when you send him ahead. Or it means they will be left and forgotten in the Fire, from (afratuhu) meaning "I left him and forgot him," as related by al-Farra', like His words: ﴿So today We forget them as they forgot the meeting of this their Day﴾ [al-A'raf: 51]. Nafi' read (mufrituna) with a kasrah on the ra', as an active participle of (afrata), meaning one who transgresses, i.e., those who exceed the limits in disobedience to God. Abu Ja'far read it with a kasrah on the doubled ra' from (farraṭa fi kadha), meaning one who falls short. Close to the verse is what He related of them in His words: ﴿And if We let him taste mercy from Us after some hardship had touched him, he would surely say, "This is mine, and I do not think the Hour will be established. And if I am returned to my Lord, surely I will have the best [reward] with Him." But We will certainly inform those who disbelieved of what they did, and We will surely make them taste a severe punishment﴾ [Fussilat: 50]. He also said: ﴿And he entered his garden while he was wronging himself. He said, "I do not think this will ever perish"﴾ [al-Kahf: 35]. ﴿And I do not think the Hour will be established. And if I am returned to my Lord, I will surely find better than it as a destination﴾ [al-Kahf: 36].

(p-3823)

The discussion on the interpretation (ta'wil) of His saying, exalted is He:

﴿By God, We certainly sent [messengers] to nations before you, but Satan made their deeds seem good to them, so he is their ally today, and theirs is a painful punishment.﴾ "Their deeds" means their disbelief, denial, and obstinacy. "So he is their ally today" means their companion, who leads them astray. Or the intended "today" is the Day of Resurrection. The word "ally" (waliyy) here means "helper." He called Satan a helper in that Day, though they will not be helped, as an exaggeration in negating help and as mockery (tahakkum), in the manner of the line: "His reproach is the sword." ﴿And theirs is a painful punishment.﴾

﴿By God, We certainly sent [messengers] to nations before you, but Satan made their deeds seem good to them, so he is their ally today, and theirs is a painful punishment.﴾ "Their deeds" means their disbelief, denial, and obstinacy. "So he is their ally today" means their companion, who leads them astray. Or the intended "today" is the Day of Resurrection. The word "ally" (waliyy) here means "helper." The Explanation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[65-66] ﴿And Allah sends down water from the sky and with it gives life to the earth after its death. Indeed in that is a sign for a people who listen﴾ ﴿And indeed for you in cattle there is a lesson. We give you to drink from what is in their bellies, from between digestive contents and blood, pure milk, palatable to the drinkers﴾ [al-Nahl: 66].

﴿And Allah sends down from the sky﴾ i.e., from the clouds (al-muzn): ﴿water, and with it gives life to the earth after its death﴾ i.e., with vegetation and crops, after its barrenness and dryness: ﴿Indeed in that is a sign for a people who listen﴾ i.e., to this reminder, and who understand the aspect of its indication.

﴿And indeed for you in cattle there is a lesson. We give you to drink from what is in their bellies, from between digestive contents﴾ [al-Nahl: 66], which is the residue in the rumen (al-kirsh) ﴿and blood, pure milk, palatable to the drinkers﴾ [al-Nahl: 66], i.e., easy to pass down their throats.

Exalted is He has shown His sign in cattle through what He mentioned, so that it may serve as evidence of His oneness and His singularity in divinity, and also as evidence of the Resurrection (al-hashr). For the grass that animals eat is only produced from water and earth. Thus the transformation of clay into plants and grass, then its conversion into blood within the animal's body, then its transformation into milk, is a greater lesson of His power to transform these lifeless substances from one attribute to another. He mentioned the pronoun in "bellies" (buṭūnihi) here and made it feminine in Surat al-Mu'minun, because al-an'am (cattle) is a collective noun (ism jam'), so its pronoun may be treated as masculine singular according to its wording, or feminine and plural according to its meaning.

And His words:

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 16, verse 67:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[67] ﴿And from the fruits of the date palms and grapevines, you take from them intoxicant and good provision. Indeed in that is a sign for a people who reason.﴾.

﴿And from the fruits of the date palms and grapevines, you take from them intoxicant and good provision. Indeed in that is a sign for a people who reason.﴾ is an explanation of His signs, exalted is He, in the fruits mentioned, and of His favour in what is drunk from them and eaten. And "sakar" (intoxicant): it is a verbal noun by which wine (khamr) is named. It has the meaning of "sukr" (intoxication), like "rushd" and "rashad" (right guidance).

Al-Farra' said: "Sakar" is wine itself. And "good provision" is raisins, dates and what is similar to them. It is not said: "Wine is forbidden, so how did God mention it in the context of blessing?" Because this surah is Meccan, and the prohibition of wine was revealed in Surat al-Ma'ida. And the revelation of this verse was at a time when wine was not forbidden. Al-Razi answered with a second answer.

(p-3825) It is: there is no need to adopt this abrogation, because He, exalted is He, mentioned the benefits of these things and addressed the polytheists with them, and wine is among their drinks, so it is a benefit with regard to them.

He said: Then, exalted is He, also alerted in this verse to its prohibition. That is because He distinguished between it and good provision in the mention, so it is necessary that intoxicant is not good provision. And there is no doubt that it is good according to desire, so it must be said: the reversal of its being good according to the Sharia. And this is only so if it is forbidden. End of quote.

Note:

Ibn Kathir said: The verse indicates equating between the intoxicant made from the palm and that made from the grape, as is the position of the majority.

In Fath al-Bayan: A group of Hanafis have taken "sakar" to mean what does not intoxicate of the beverages (anbidha), and what has had two-thirds reduced by cooking until it becomes strong to the limit of intoxication. As in al-Kashshaf.

They said: God only bestows favour upon His servants with what He has made lawful for them, not with what He has forbidden to them. And this is rejected by the sound, mass-transmitted hadiths, on the assumption that it came later than the verse of the prohibition of wine. End of quote.

This is not the place to expand on that. Ibn Kathir said: The mention of reason is appropriate here in His saying: ﴿for a people who reason﴾, for it is the noblest of what is in man. For this reason God forbade this community intoxicating drinks, to preserve their minds. End of quote.

When He, exalted is He, made clear that the extraction of milk from the livestock, and the extraction of intoxicant and good provision from the fruits of the date palms and grapevines, are overwhelming proofs and dazzling evidences that this world has one God, capable, choosing and wise, He guided to His shining sign in the Bee also, by His saying, glorified is He:

(p-3826)

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 16, verses 68–69:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[68–69] ﴿And your Lord inspired to the bee: "Take for yourself among the mountains, houses, and among the trees and that which they construct."﴾ ﴿Then eat from all the fruits and follow the ways of your Lord, made easy." There emerges from their bellies a drink, varying in its colors, wherein is healing for people. Indeed in that is a sign for a people who give thought.﴾ [al-Nahl: 69].

﴿And your Lord inspired to the bee: "Take for yourself among the mountains, houses, and among the trees and that which they construct."﴾ What is meant by "inspiration" (wahy) is guidance (ilham) and direction (hidayah) to building those wondrous hexagonal houses, of equal sides, none exceeding another, the like of which is impossible for humans except with tools and instruments. God, exalted is He, guided them to build houses in which they take shelter in three places: the mountains, the trees, and the houses of people, where they "construct" (ya'rishun), meaning they build trellises (al-'urush), plural of (ʿarsh), which is the shelter under which one gains shade, like an arbour (ʿarish). The bee has no hive except in these places: the mountains, the trees, and the houses of people. Most of their hives are in the mountains, which is what is mentioned first in the verse, then in the trees, less so, and then in the third place is fewest.

So the bee is of two kinds: wild (jabaliyyah), which dwells in the mountains and wastelands and which no person tends; and domestic (ahliyyah), which takes shelter in houses and is tended in hives. Among the marvels of its inspiration is that it takes up its houses before its pasture. It first takes a dwelling; once a dwelling is settled for it, it goes out from it, forages, eats from the fruits, and then returns to its houses. God, exalted is He, has indicated this by His saying: ﴿Then eat from all the fruits﴾ [al-Nahl: 69], meaning from every fruit you desire, sweet and bitter. The generality here is customary, or the word (kull) is for abundance, or it is a general term specified by custom. Were the matter left to its apparent sense, it would be permissible, for the command to eat from all fruits does not necessarily entail eating from them all, since the command is for permission and allowance.

(p-3827) A subtle point:

The particle (min) was preferred in His saying ﴿from the mountains﴾ etc., over (fi), to indicate the meaning of partiality, and that their houses are not built on every mountain, every tree, and everything that is trellised, nor in every place of them. Al-Zamakhshari drew attention to this.

Al-Nasir said: This meaning which he pointed out, in the partiality of (min) connected to the taking of houses, is embellished by the unrestricted eating. It is as if God, exalted is He, left eating to their desire and choice, and did not restrict them in it, while He restricted them regarding the houses and commanded them to take them in some places and not others, because the benefit of the eater is achieved absolutely through the continuous availability of what it desires. As for the houses, their benefit is not achieved in every place. For this meaning (thumma) was used, to mark the difference between restriction regarding the taking of houses and the unrestricted permission to consume the fruits, as you would say: "Be mindful of what is lawful in what you eat, then eat whatever you wish." So the intermediary (thumma) marks the difference between restriction and permission. Glory be to the Subtle, the All-Aware.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then follow the ways of your Lord, made easy﴾ [al-Nahl: 69], meaning: the paths which He inspired and made you understand in the work of making honey. So "ways" (subul) is either a metaphor for the methods of work and their kinds, or is taken literally. That is: when you have eaten the fruits in distant places, return to your houses by the ways of your Lord; they will not be rugged for you, nor will you go astray in them. "Made easy" (dhululan) is the plural of (dhalul), a state (hal) of "ways", meaning: made smooth, which God has made easy and facilitated for you. Thus it travels through this vast atmosphere, the wide deserts, valleys, and towering mountains. Then each one returns to its own house, never deviating from it to the right or to the left.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿There emerges from their bellies a drink﴾ [al-Nahl: 69] is a new sentence (isti'naf), turned from addressing the bee, to explain what appears from them of God's wondrous creation, enumerating the blessings, drawing attention to lessons, and guiding to the great signs from this weak creature. Honey is called a drink (sharab) because it is drunk with water and other things. ﴿Varying in its colors﴾ [Fatir: 28], meaning: some of it is white, yellow, and red, due to the difference in what they eat of the blossoms or in their temperaments. ﴿Wherein is healing for people﴾ [al-Nahl: 69], because it is among the remedies and medicines for some diseases. It enters into most of what healing is sought in, and confections (ma'ajin); few confections are there in which physicians have not mentioned honey. Now sugar has taken its place, due to its abundance relative to it.

In the two Sahihs, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, that "a man came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: 'My brother's stomach has loosened.' He said: 'Give him honey to drink.' He went and gave him honey to drink, then came and said: 'O Messenger of Allah! I gave him honey to drink, and it only increased his looseness.' He said: 'Go and give him honey to drink.' He went and gave him honey to drink, then came and said: 'O Messenger of Allah! It only increased his looseness.' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Allah has spoken the truth, and your brother's belly has lied. Go and give him honey to drink.' He went and gave him honey to drink, and he was cured."

Ibn Kathir said: Some scholars of medicine said: this man had accumulated waste matter. When he gave him honey, being hot, it dissolved the matter and it hastened to be expelled, so it increased his loosening. The Bedouin thought this harmed him, though it was beneficial for his brother. Then he gave it again and the dissolving and expelling increased; then he gave it again, and likewise. When the corrupt waste harmful to the body was expelled, his belly became firm, his temperament was restored, and illnesses and pains were removed by the blessing of his ﷺ instruction. End of quote.

In al-'Inayah by al-Shihab here there is a story about the classes of physicians which supports the story of the Bedouin; consult it.

﴿Indeed in that is a sign for a people who give thought﴾ [al-Nahl: 69], meaning: so that they may take heed and reason toward His oneness, glory be to Him, and His singularity in divinity, and that it is He who inspired these weak creatures, so they know the places where dews fall, from beyond the deserts, so they alight on every fragrant heat and graceful flower, then return from them with what they keep as saliva and expel as drink.

(p-3829) Al-Hujjat al-Ghazali (in al-Ihya) said: Look at the bee, how God inspired it until it took houses from the mountains, and how He extracted from its saliva the wax and the honey, and made one a light and the other a cure. Then if you contemplate the wonders of its affairs in taking the flowers and blossoms, its avoidance of impurities and filth, and its obedience to one of its own, the largest in body, which is its leader, and then what God has subjected for its leader of justice and fairness among them, such that at the doorway of the hive whatever among them falls upon an impurity is killed, you would be astonished at that, if you were perceptive within yourself, free from concern for your belly and private parts, and from the desires of your soul in opposing your peers and befriending your brothers. Then leave all of that aside and look at its building a house of wax, and its choice from all shapes of the hexagonal shape. It does not build its house round, nor square, nor pentagonal, but hexagonal, for a property in the hexagonal shape which the understanding of the geometer falls short of grasping. That is: the most spacious and advantageous of shapes is the circle and what approaches it. The square leaves wasted corners. The bee's form is round-elongated. So it abandoned the square so that no corners remain empty. Then if it had built them round, there would remain wasted gaps outside the houses, for round shapes when gathered do not pack together tightly, and no shape among those with corners is closer in enclosing than the circle. Then the whole assembly packs together such that after their gathering no gap remains except in the hexagon. This is the property of this shape. So look how God, exalted is He, inspired the bee, despite its small body, to this, out of kindness toward it and care for its existence in what it needs, so that its life may be pleasant. Glory be to Him, how great His majesty and how vast His kindness and favor. In its nature is that some of them flee from others, and some fight others in the hives, and it stings whoever approaches the hive, and sometimes the stung one dies. When some of them die inside the hives, the living remove them outside. Also in its nature is cleanliness; therefore its waste is expelled from the hive, because it is foul-smelling. It knows the seasons of spring and autumn, and what it makes in spring is finer. The young is more industrious than the old. It drinks water that is clear and sweet, seeking it wherever it is. It eats of the honey only a sufficient amount. When honey runs low in the hive, it sprinkles it with water so that it increases, fearing for itself its depletion; for if it runs out, the bees ravage the houses of kings and the houses of males, and sometimes they kill whatever is there.

(p-3830) A wise man of the Greeks said to his disciples: "Be like the bees in the hives." They said: "And how are the bees in the hives?" He said: "They do not leave an idler among them without expelling him, removing him far from the hive, because he narrows the place, consumes the honey, and teaches the active to be lazy."

The bee sheds its skin like snakes. Pleasant, melodious sounds agree with it, and it is harmed by weevils. Its remedy is that a handful of salt be placed in every hive, and that it be opened once a month and fumigated with cow dung. In its nature is that whenever it flies from the hive, it forages and then returns, so every bee returns to its place without missing it. Thus in (Hayat al-Hayawan).

Imam al-Ghazali also mentioned in the book (al-Hikmah fi Khalq al-Makhlukat): that God, exalted is He, appointed for the bees a leader whom they follow and by whom they are guided in what they obtain of their sustenance. If there appears alongside the leader they follow another leader of their kind, one of them kills the other, for an evident benefit, namely fear of dispersal; for if there were two leaders, and each took a different path, the bees would scatter behind them. Then they were inspired to graze on moisture upon the flowers, which then transforms in their bellies into honey. Thus from this subjection is known what it contains of benefits for the servants, a drink wherein is healing for people, as He, glory be to Him and exalted, has informed. In it is nourishment and sweetness for the servants. In it is also a great surplus of sustenance placed for the benefit of the children of Adam. It is like the surplus of milk, which was created for the welfare of the offspring of animals and their sustenance. What exceeds of that contains blessing and abundance by which people benefit. Then consider what the bee carries of wax on its legs, to store the honey in it and preserve it. You hardly find a vessel better at preserving honey than wax in the wings. Look at this little fly: is there in its knowledge and power the gathering of wax together with honey? Or has it such knowledge that it arranges the preservation of honey for a long period by its settling in the wax and its safekeeping in the mountains and trees, in places where it preserves it and does not spoil! Then consider its going out by day to graze and its returning in the evening to its places, having carried what sustains its strength and what exceeds it. In the arrangement of its houses there is wisdom in their construction, a guard for what it casts out of its bellies of honey, (p-3831) and it has another aspect in which it makes its excrement distant from the places of honey. And there is other than this of what God alone has knowledge.

Abu al-Su'ud said: When He, glory be to Him, mentioned among the wonders of the states of what He mentioned of water, plants, livestock, and bees, He pointed to some wonders of the states of humans from the beginning of their life to its end and their transformations in between. The scholars have defined the stages of life as four: the first: the age of growth and increase; the second: the age of standing, which is the age of youth; the third: the age of slight decline, which is the age of middle years; and the fourth: the age of great decline, which is the age of old age. Then He, glory be to Him, said:
