When some of them die inside the hives, the living remove them outside. Also in its nature is cleanliness; therefore its waste is expelled from the hive, because it is foul-smelling. It knows the seasons of spring and autumn, and what it makes in spring is finer. The young is more industrious than the old. It drinks water that is clear and sweet, seeking it wherever it is. It eats of the honey only a sufficient amount. When honey runs low in the hive, it sprinkles it with water so that it increases, fearing for itself its depletion; for if it runs out, the bees ravage the houses of kings and the houses of males, and sometimes they kill whatever is there.

(p-3830) A wise man of the Greeks said to his disciples: "Be like the bees in the hives." They said: "And how are the bees in the hives?" He said: "They do not leave an idler among them without expelling him, removing him far from the hive, because he narrows the place, consumes the honey, and teaches the active to be lazy."

The bee sheds its skin like snakes. Pleasant, melodious sounds agree with it, and it is harmed by weevils. Its remedy is that a handful of salt be placed in every hive, and that it be opened once a month and fumigated with cow dung. In its nature is that whenever it flies from the hive, it forages and then returns, so every bee returns to its place without missing it. Thus in (Hayat al-Hayawan).

Imam al-Ghazali also mentioned in the book (al-Hikmah fi Khalq al-Makhlukat): that God, exalted is He, appointed for the bees a leader whom they follow and by whom they are guided in what they obtain of their sustenance. If there appears alongside the leader they follow another leader of their kind, one of them kills the other, for an evident benefit, namely fear of dispersal; for if there were two leaders, and each took a different path, the bees would scatter behind them. Then they were inspired to graze on moisture upon the flowers, which then transforms in their bellies into honey. Thus from this subjection is known what it contains of benefits for the servants, a drink wherein is healing for people, as He, glory be to Him and exalted, has informed. In it is nourishment and sweetness for the servants. In it is also a great surplus of sustenance placed for the benefit of the children of Adam. It is like the surplus of milk, which was created for the welfare of the offspring of animals and their sustenance. What exceeds of that contains blessing and abundance by which people benefit. Then consider what the bee carries of wax on its legs, to store the honey in it and preserve it. You hardly find a vessel better at preserving honey than wax in the wings. Look at this little fly: is there in its knowledge and power the gathering of wax together with honey? Or has it such knowledge that it arranges the preservation of honey for a long period by its settling in the wax and its safekeeping in the mountains and trees, in places where it preserves it and does not spoil! Then consider its going out by day to graze and its returning in the evening to its places, having carried what sustains its strength and what exceeds it. In the arrangement of its houses there is wisdom in their construction, a guard for what it casts out of its bellies of honey, (p-3831) and it has another aspect in which it makes its excrement distant from the places of honey. And there is other than this of what God alone has knowledge.

Abu al-Su'ud said: When He, glory be to Him, mentioned among the wonders of the states of what He mentioned of water, plants, livestock, and bees, He pointed to some wonders of the states of humans from the beginning of their life to its end and their transformations in between. The scholars have defined the stages of life as four: the first: the age of growth and increase; the second: the age of standing, which is the age of youth; the third: the age of slight decline, which is the age of middle years; and the fourth: the age of great decline, which is the age of old age. Then He, glory be to Him, said:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[70-71] ﴿And Allah created you, then causes you to die; and among you is one who is returned to the most abject age, so that he knows, after knowledge, nothing. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Competent.﴾ ﴿And Allah has favored some of you over others in provision. But those who were favored would not give their provision to those whom their right hands possess, so that they would be equal therein. Then is it the favor of Allah they deny?﴾ [An-Nahl: 71].

﴿And Allah created you⦆ i.e., brought you into being from nothing. ﴿Then causes you to die; and among you is one who is returned to the most abject age⦆ i.e., its weakest and most degraded state, which is senility (al-haram). His saying, exalted is He, ﴿so that he knows, after knowledge, nothing⦆: the lam here is of consequence and outcome (al-lam li'l-sayrurah wa'l-'aqibah). That is: he becomes, if he was knowing, ignorant; so He shows you from His power that just as He is able to transfer him from knowledge to ignorance, He is able to restore him to life after his death.

In (al-'Inayah) it is said: His being no longer knowing after his knowledge is a metonymy (kinayah) for forgetfulness, because the forgetful person knows a thing and then forgets it, so he no longer knows what he once knew. Or "knowing" is taken in the sense of perception and rational understanding, and the meaning is: his perception and understanding do not advance, because the young person is in progress, while the old man is in stagnation and decline.

In (al-Kashshaf): so that he reaches a state resembling the condition of childhood in forgetfulness, and that he knows a thing and then quickly forgets it, so that if asked about it he does not know it. It was also said: lest he understand, after his first understanding, anything; and it was said: lest he know an increase of knowledge over his first knowledge. And (shay'an) is in the accusative either as a verbal noun (masdar) or as an object. It is permissible that there be a case of contention (tanazu') between (ya'lama) and ('ilmin), and that the object of ('ilmin) be omitted for the purpose of generality. That is: he does not know any thing after he had known many things. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Competent⦆.

﴿And Allah has favored some of you over others in provision⦆ [An-Nahl: 71], i.e., He made you differ in it, so He gave you provision better than what He gave your slaves, though they are human beings like you. ﴿But those who were favored⦆ [An-Nahl: 71], i.e., in provision, and they are the owners: ﴿would not give their provision to those whom their right hands possess⦆ [An-Nahl: 71], i.e., by giving it to them; ﴿so that they would be equal therein⦆ [An-Nahl: 71], i.e., so that they would be equal with their slaves in provision.

The verse is an example struck for those who set up partners with Him, exalted is He. That is: you do not make equal between yourselves and your slaves in what I have bestowed upon you, nor do you make them partners in it, nor do you accept that for yourselves. How then do you accept that you make My servants partners in divinity and in exaltation? As He said in another place: ﴿He has struck for you an example from yourselves: Do you have among those whom your right hands possess any partners in what We have provided you, so that you are equal therein, fearing them as you fear one another?﴾ [Ar-Rum: 28].

﴿Then is it the favor of Allah they deny?⦆ [An-Nahl: 71], i.e., so that they associate with Him others, while He is the one who bestowed favor upon them. Or: since they deny such conclusive proofs after He has bestowed them upon them?! For there is no favor upon the world greater than the establishment of proofs and the clarification of paths through the sending of messengers.

On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[72–74] ﴿And Allah has made for you spouses from among yourselves, and made for you, from your spouses, sons and grandchildren, and provided you with good things. Do they then believe in falsehood and disbelieve in the favour of Allah?﴾ ﴿And they worship, besides Allah, that which possesses for them no provision from the heavens and the earth, nor are they able﴾ [al-Nahl: 73] ﴿So do not strike forth comparisons for Allah. Indeed, Allah knows, and you do not know﴾ [al-Nahl: 74].

﴿And Allah has made for you spouses from among yourselves﴾ i.e., females of your own kind and form, as spouses, that you may find comfort in them and that affection, companionship and mercy may be achieved. ﴿And made for you, from your spouses, sons and grandchildren﴾ i.e., daughters and sons, and sons' sons. ﴿And provided you with good things. Do they then believe in falsehood﴾ — which is the benefit of the idols and their intercession. ﴿And disbelieve in the favour of Allah?﴾ i.e., in attributing His favours to the idols, or in forbidding what He has made lawful for them.

﴿And they worship, besides Allah, that which possesses for them no provision from the heavens and the earth, nor anything﴾ [al-Nahl: 73] i.e., of rain or plants. The word ﴿shay'an﴾ (anything) is in the accusative as an object of "rizq" (provision) if the latter is a verbal noun; if it is taken as a noun for "that which is provided," then ﴿shay'an﴾ is a substitute for it, meaning "a little." The phrase ﴿from the heavens﴾ is connected to "yamliku" (possesses) if "rizq" is a verbal noun, or it is a qualifier of ﴿rizqan﴾ (provision). ﴿Nor are they able﴾ [al-Nahl: 73] i.e., to take possession of it; or there is no ability for them at all; or the pronoun refers to the polytheists, meaning: nor are they able, although they are living beings who act, so how about inanimate matter?!

﴿So do not strike forth comparisons for Allah﴾ [al-Nahl: 74] i.e., do not make for Him rivals and likenesses. The striking of a likeness (*darb al-mathal*) carries the meaning of "making." The word ﴿al-amthal﴾ is the plural of *mithl* (with a kasra and then a sukun) according to this reading; it is said to be the plural of *mathal* (with two fatahs). The verse is a figurative, illustrative metaphor for associating partners with Him, in which the one who associates the partner with Him, who likens Him to His creation, is placed in the position of the one who strikes the likeness. The deluded one who makes the comparison likens an attribute to an attribute and an essence to an essence, just as the one who strikes a likeness does. It is as if it were said: "And do not associate partners." He turned away from this to what has been mentioned, indicating generality in the prohibition against likening Him in attributes and essence. In the word ﴿al-amthal﴾ (the likenesses), for One who has no likeness, there is a severe reproach for the evil of their deed. Thus in *Sharh al-Kashshaf*.

﴿Indeed, Allah knows, and you do not know﴾ [al-Nahl: 74] i.e., He knows the ugliness of what you associate, and you do not know it. Had you known it, you would not have dared to do it, so this is a reason for the prohibition. Or: He knows the reality of things, and you do not know it, so leave your opinion and your analogy in favour of His text. When He forbade them from striking the practical likeness, which is association, He followed it with an unveiling for the discerning, concerning their state in that heedlessness and the state of those who followed them, with His statement, glorified is He:

The discussion of the words of God Most High:

[75] ﴿God strikes a parable: a slave owned, who has no power over anything; and one whom We have provided with goodly provision from Us, so he spends from it secretly and openly. Are they equal? Praise be to God! But most of them do not know.﴾

﴿God strikes a parable: a slave owned, who has no power over anything; and one whom We have provided with goodly provision from Us, so he spends from it secretly and openly. Are they equal? Praise be to God! But most of them do not know.﴾ Meaning: the likeness of these people in their associating partners with God is like that of one who equates a owned slave, incapable of disposing of anything, with a free owner who disposes of his property as he wishes. There is no equality between them, although they are alike in being human and in being created by God, glorified and exalted is He. How, then, is the assumption about the Lord of the worlds, when they associate with Him the most incapable of creatures?! The phrasing ﴿and whom We have provided﴾ etc. instead of "owner" serves to alert that what is in his hand is from God's bounty and provision, and to remind him of spending from it in secret and openly, so that he acts in accordance with God's command regarding it.

(p-3835) God's words: ﴿Praise be to God﴾ mean: for what He guided His friends to and bestowed upon them of monotheism. Or, all praise belongs to Him; nothing among the idols deserves it. Or, praise be to God for the strength of this argument and the clarity of the proof, but most of them do not know it, although it is at the utmost clarity and the peak of its manifestness.

And the words of God Most High:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[76] ﴿And Allah presents an example: two men, one of them dumb, unable to do anything, and a burden upon his master; wherever he directs him, he brings no good. Is he equal to one who enjoins justice and is on a straight path?﴾

﴿And Allah presents an example﴾ — that is, another example that indicates what the previous example indicated, in a clearer manner: ﴿two men, one of them dumb﴾ — that is, mute: ﴿unable to do anything﴾ — that is, of what the articulate speaker, who expresses what is in his self, is able to do: ﴿and a burden upon his master﴾ — that is, a weight upon the one who manages his affairs, due to his not caring to establish the welfare of himself: ﴿wherever he directs him, he brings no good﴾ — that is, wherever he sends him on a matter, he does not bring success in it nor sufficiency in his concern: ﴿Is he equal to one who enjoins justice﴾ — that is, one who is eloquent and articulate, possessing sufficiency and right guidance, so that he benefits people by urging them to justice, which encompasses all virtues.

﴿And he is on a straight path﴾ — that is, in himself, together with what has been mentioned of his general benefit, he is upon a righteous course and an upright religion, not turning toward any goal without reaching it with the nearest and easiest effort.

Al-Azhari said: Exalted is He presented an example for the idol which they worshipped, which is unable to do anything, and is thus a burden upon its master, for he carries it when he travels, moving it from place to place. So Allah, Exalted is He, says: Is this idol, the burden, equal to one who enjoins justice? It is an interrogative whose meaning is reproach, as if He said: Do not equate the idol with the Creator, Majestic is His majesty. End.

Al-Zamakhshari alluded to this with his saying: This is an example which Allah struck for Himself, and for what He bestows upon His servants and encompasses them with, together with the traces of His mercy, His kindnesses, and His religious and worldly blessings; and for the idols, which are dead, neither harming nor benefiting. End.

Al-Razi objected to interpreting it as referring to the idol, saying that the description as a man, as mute, as a burden, and as one who turns toward the directions of benefits, prevents taking them as referring to an idol. Likewise, the description in the second case as being on a straight path prevents taking it as referring to Allah, Exalted is He. End.

It may be answered: the first descriptions, although apparent in a human being (and the basic sense of an unqualified expression is that which comes to mind first, which is the literal meaning), nonetheless the context redirects them to the idol, because the verses are explaining the baseness of what is worshipped besides Him, Exalted is He, and that it is not fit for divinity in any respect, because of the attributes of deficiency in it. As for the description in His saying ﴿on a straight path﴾, it is like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, my Lord is on a straight path﴾ [Hud: 56], so the attribution is valid.

Then I saw that the Imam Ibn al-Qayyim, in (A'lam al-Muwaqqi'in), in his discussion of the parables of the Qur'an, concerning these two examples, has something that supports what we have relied upon, where he said, in substance:

As for the first example, namely His saying: ﴿Allah presents an example: a slave owned﴾ [al-Nahl: 75] to the end of the verse, Allah, Glorified is He, struck it for Himself and for the idols. Allah, Glorified is He, is the Owner of everything. He spends as He wills upon His servants, secretly and openly, by night and by day. His right hand is full, not diminished by expenditure, pouring forth night and day. The idols are owned, powerless, unable to do anything; so how do they make them partners with Me and worship them besides Me, with this great disparity and clear difference? This is the saying of Mujahid and others.

Ibn 'Abbas said: It is an example Allah struck for the believer and the disbeliever. The example of the believer is that of one to whom Allah has given good provision from His good, so he spends from it upon himself and others, secretly and openly. The disbeliever is like a slave owned, (p-3837) powerless, unable to do anything, for he has no good with him. Do the two men become equal in the sight of any of the intelligent? The first saying is more akin to the intended meaning, for it is more evident in refuting polytheism, clearer to the addressee, greater in establishing proof, and closer in connection with His saying: ﴿And they worship besides Allah what does not own for them any provision from the heavens and earth, anything, and they are not able﴾ [al-Nahl: 73], ﴿So do not strike for Allah examples. Indeed, Allah knows, and you do not know﴾ [al-Nahl: 74]. Then He said: ﴿Allah presents an example: a slave owned, who is unable to do anything﴾ [al-Nahl: 75]. Among the necessary implications and rulings of this example is that the believing monotheist is one to whom He has given good provision from Himself, while the disbelieving polytheist is like the owned slave who is unable to do anything. This is what the example alerts to and guides toward. Ibn 'Abbas mentioned it as an alert to its intention, not that the verse is restricted to it. So contemplate it, for you will find it frequent in the words of Ibn 'Abbas and others among the early generation in understanding the Qur'an. One may suppose that this is the meaning of the verse, which has no meaning other than it, and so he repeats it as his saying.

As for the second example, it is an example Allah, Glorified and Exalted is He, struck for Himself and for what they worship besides Him as well. The idol which is worshipped besides Him is like a mute man who neither understands nor speaks. Rather, he is mute of heart and tongue, having lost both inner and outer speech; yet he is powerless, unable to do anything at all. On this basis, wherever you send him, he does not bring you good, nor does he fulfill any need for you. Allah, Glorified is He, is Living, Powerful, Speaking, who enjoins justice, and He is on a straight path. This is a description of Him with utmost perfection and praise. For His commanding justice, which is the truth, implies that He, Glorified is He, is Knowing of it, Teaching it, pleased with it, commanding His servants with it, loving its people, and commands nothing other than it; rather He is exalted above its opposite, which is oppression, injustice, folly, and falsehood. Indeed His command and His law are entirely justice. The people of justice are His friends and beloved, and they are those who sit near Him at His right hand, upon pulpits of light. His command with justice encompasses both the legislative religious command and the decreed cosmic command, and both are justice in which there is no injustice in any way, as in the authentic hadith: "O Allah, I am Your servant, son of Your servant, son of Your handmaid; my forelock is in Your hand, Your judgment prevails over me, Your decree over me is just." So His decree (p-3838) is His cosmic command: ﴿Indeed, His command when He intends a thing is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is﴾ [Ya-Sin: 82], so He commands only with truth and justice. His decree and His predestination which subsists in Him are truth and justice. And if in the decreed and predestined there is what is oppression and injustice, the decree is other than the decreed, and the predestination is other than the predestined. Then Glorified is He informed that He is on a straight path, and this is like the saying of His messenger Shu'ayb: ﴿Indeed I have put my trust in Allah, my Lord and your Lord. There is no creature but that He holds its forelock. Indeed my Lord is on a straight path﴾ [Hud: 56]. His saying ﴿there is no creature but that He holds its forelock﴾ [Hud: 56] is like His saying "my forelock is in Your hand," and His saying ﴿Indeed my Lord is on a straight path﴾ [Hud: 56] is like His saying "Your decree over me is just." The first is His dominion, and the second is His praiseworthiness. To Him belongs dominion, and to Him belongs praise. His being, Glorified is He, on a straight path requires that He says only the truth, commands only justice, and does only what is benefit, mercy, wisdom and justice. So He is upon the truth in His sayings and His deeds. He does not decree upon the servant that by which he would be wronged, nor is he seized for other than his sin. He does not diminish from his good deeds anything, nor does He load upon him the evil deeds of others which he did not do and to which he did not contribute anything; nor does He punish anyone for the sin of another, nor does He ever do what is not praiseworthy, nor what does not bring praise to Him, and does not have in it praiseworthy outcomes and desired ends. For His being on a straight path refuses all of that.

Muhammad ibn Jarir al-Tabari said: His saying ﴿Indeed my Lord is on a straight path﴾ [Hud: 56] means: Indeed my Lord is on the way of truth, rewarding the one who does good among His creatures for his good, and the one who does evil for his evil, not wronging any of them, and not accepting from them anything but Islam for Him and faith in Him.

Then it is reported from Mujahid, via Shibl ibn Abi Najih, from him: ﴿Indeed my Lord is on a straight path﴾ [Hud: 56] — he said: the truth. Likewise Ibn Jurayj transmitted it from him.

(p-3839) A group said: it is like His saying: ﴿Indeed your Lord is ever watchful﴾ [al-Fajr: 14], and this is a difference of expression, for His being watchful is the recompensing of the doer of good for his good and the doer of evil for his evil.

A group said: there is an ellipsis in the speech, its estimate being: Indeed my Lord urges you upon a straight path and exhorts you to it. As for these, if they intend that this is the meaning of the verse, then it is not as they claimed, and there is no evidence for this assumed element. Glorified is He has distinguished between His being one who commands justice and His being on a straight path. And if they intend that His urging upon the straight path is among the implications of His being on a straight path, then they are correct.

Another group said: the meaning of His being on a straight path is that the return of servants and of all affairs is to Allah, and nothing of them escapes Him. As for these, if they intend that this is the meaning of the verse, then it is not so. And if they intend that this is among the necessary implications of His being on a straight path, and among its requirements and consequences, then it is true.

Another group said: its meaning is that everything is under His power and domination, in His dominion and grasp. Though this is true, it is not the meaning of the verse. Shu'ayb distinguished between His saying ﴿there is no creature but that He holds its forelock﴾ [Hud: 56] and His saying ﴿Indeed my Lord is on a straight path﴾ [Hud: 56], and these are two independent meanings.

So the saying of Mujahid is the correct one. It is the view of the imams of tafsir. Arabic does not admit any other reading except with strain.

Jarir said praising Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz:

Commander of the believers, upon a path, straight, when the watering-places deviate.

And Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿Whomever Allah wills to misguide, He misguides; and whomever He wills, He places upon a straight path﴾ [al-An'am: 39]. (p-3840) And if He, Glorified is He, is the One who placed His messengers and their followers upon the straight path in their sayings and deeds, then He, Glorified is He, is more worthy of being upon a straight path in His saying and His doing. And if the path of the messengers and their followers is conformity with His command, then His path upon which He, Glorified is He, is that which His praiseworthiness, perfection and glory require of His speaking the truth and His acting. And success is from Allah.

In the verse there is a second saying, equal to the first: that it is an example Allah struck for the believer and the disbeliever. What this saying involves has already been mentioned. And success is from Allah. End, verbatim. And His saying, Exalted is He:

The Interpretation of His Words, exalted is He:

[77] ﴿And to Allah belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth. And the matter of the Hour is but as a glance of the eye, or it is nearer. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent.﴾

﴿And to Allah belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth. And the matter of the Hour is but as a glance of the eye, or it is nearer. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent.﴾

The verse is either a response to their hastening of what they were promised, or to their slowness in regarding the Hour, or an explanation of His perfection in knowledge and power, as an allusion that their deities are devoid of both. He pointed to the first with His words: ﴿And to Allah belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth﴾, meaning: the knowledge of what is hidden in them from the servants and what is concealed from them is exclusive to Him. Or their unseen: it is the Day of Resurrection, for its knowledge is hidden from its inhabitants, and none of them has come to know it. He pointed to the second with His words: ﴿And the matter of the Hour is but as a glance of the eye, or it is nearer﴾. And "the Hour" (al-sa'ah) is the time at which the Resurrection occurs. And "al-lamh" (the glance) is looking quickly; that is, like the return of the gaze from the top of the pupil to its bottom. "Or it is nearer" than that, meaning: swifter in time, such that it occurs within a part of its time. In this is, of the perfection of the affirmation of His exalted power, what is not hidden. And His words: ﴿Indeed, Allah is over all things competent﴾ is a justification for it, indicating that His exalted capabilities are not finite, and that what is mentioned is only a part of them. And His exalted words:

(p-3841)

The discourse on the interpretation of His words, Exalted is He:

[78-79] ﴿And God brought you forth from the wombs of your mothers, knowing nothing, and made for you hearing, sight and hearts, that perhaps you would give thanks.﴾ ﴿Have they not regarded the birds subjected in the expanse of the sky? None holds them up except God. Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe.﴾ [al-Nahl: 79].

﴿And God brought you forth from the wombs of your mothers, knowing nothing﴾ is coordinated (ʿatf) with His words, ﴿And God made for you spouses from yourselves﴾ [al-Nahl: 72]. It is linked with them in the string of proofs of divine oneness (tawhid), from His words, ﴿And God sent down water from the sky﴾ [al-Nahl: 65], and His words, ﴿And God created you﴾ [al-Nahl: 70], and His words, ﴿And God has favoured some of you over others﴾ [al-Nahl: 71]. This is what Abu al-Su'ud conveyed. The word (shay'an) is in the accusative either as a verbal noun (maṣdar) or as the object of (taʿlamūna, "you know"), and the negation falls upon it. That is: you know nothing at all of the right of the Benefactor or of anything else.

﴿And He made for you hearing﴾, meaning that by it you perceive sounds; ﴿and sight﴾, by which you perceive visible things; ﴿and hearts﴾, meaning the intellects (ʿuqūl). ﴿That perhaps you would give thanks﴾, meaning that you would employ them in that for which they were created: the affirmation of divine oneness, contemplation (iʿtibar) through them, and walking in accordance with the cosmic laws (sunan kawniyya). Then, Exalted is He, drew attention to His sign in His creation of birds, with His words:

﴿Have they not regarded the birds subjected﴾ [al-Nahl: 79], meaning made subservient, ﴿in the expanse of the sky? None holds them up except God﴾ [al-Nahl: 79], meaning that nothing holds them up in the air without being attached to any substance or relying on any heavy body, except Him, glory be to Him. ﴿Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe﴾ [al-Nahl: 79].

Al-Ḥujjat al-Ghazali (Proof of Islam al-Ghazali) said in his book "The Wisdom in the Creation of Created Things", concerning the wisdom in birds in this verse, the following, or something like it:

Know, may God have mercy upon you, that God, Exalted is He, created the bird and perfected it with a wisdom that requires lightness for flight, and did not create in it anything that would weigh it down. He created in it what it needs and what its sustenance and the regulation of its nourishment depend upon, and He apportioned to each of its limbs what suits it. If a limb is soft, or dry, or between these, the nourishment directed to each limb is what is fitting for it.

[p. 3842] So He created for the bird two legs without two hands, due to the necessity of its walking and moving about, and to assist it in raising itself from the ground at the time of its flight. He made the lower part (of the foot) broad so that it may stand firm on the ground, and it is a sole (khuff) in it, or some toes created from thin yet firm skin, in proportion to the skin of its shanks. He made the skin of its shanks thick and very well-formed, so that it may dispense with feathers in heat and cold. It was part of the wisdom that it was created in this form, because in its grazing and seeking its food it cannot do without places where there is mud and water; had its shanks been covered with feathers, they would have been harmed by the wetness and soiling. So He, glory be to Him, made it independent of feathers in a place where they would be unsuitable, so that the legs are purely for flight.

As for the birds He created with long legs, their necks were made long so that they may reach their food without hardship with them. For if their legs were long and their necks short, it would not be possible for them to graze in the wild lands or in the marshes without falling on their chests. Often, a long beak is also given together with a long neck, so that its reaching its food is made easier. Had its neck been long and its legs short, its neck would have burdened it and its grazing would have been disturbed.

He created its chest and its rounded part wrapped around a bone in the shape of a half-circle, so that it may cut through the air without effort. Likewise, the tips of its wings are rounded, to help it in flight.

He made for each species of bird a beak suited to its grazing and fit for what it feeds upon, whether by cutting, picking up, digging or other means. Among them is the talon-like beak for cutting, which is specific to the predators and whose food is flesh. Among them is the broad beak with serrated sides, which closes firmly upon what it picks up. Among them is the beak moderate in picking up and eating greens. Among them is the long beak which He made hard and strong, like bone, yet with some flexibility, though not as bone is, because of the great need to use it; it occupies the place of teeth in other animals.

Glory be to Him, He strengthened the base of the feather and made it a stalk (qaṣab) arranged in what suits it of the firm skin in the wings, and for the sake of the great amount of flying, and because the motion of flight is strong, it needs perfection for the sake of the feather. He made its feathers a shield against what harms it of heat or cold, and an aid to the air passing through them for flight. He specifically gave the wings the strongest, firmest and most perfectly formed feathers, because of the great demand of need for them. He made on the rest of its body other feathers as clothing, protection and beauty for it.

He made in its feathers, as part of the wisdom, that wetness does not spoil them and dirt does not soil them. If water reaches it, the easiest shaking (infitāḍ) [p. 3843] casts off its wetness, and it returns to its lightness. He made for it a single outlet for laying eggs and for the expulsion of its waste, for the sake of its lightness. He created the feathers of its tail as an aid to keeping it steady in its flight; were it not for them, its wings would tilt it to the right and left during flight. So they serve it as the rudder of a ship, by which its course is kept straight.

He created in its nature caution as a protection for its safety. Since its food it swallows whole without chewing, He made for some of them a hard beak with which it cuts the flesh, standing in place of what is cut with a knife. It comes to swallow what it eats whole. It is aided by an excess of heat in its belly, which grinds the food into a paste, so that it has no need of chewing or the weight of teeth. This is seen in the grape seed and others: it comes out of the bellies of animals intact, but is crushed in the bellies of birds.

Then He created it to lay eggs and not to give birth to live young, so that it would not be weighed down from flight. For if its young were formed inside its body until their creation was complete, it would be burdened by them and hindered from rising for flight. Do you not see how He arranged every thing of His creation with what suits it of wisdom?! The end, summarised.

Then Allah, Exalted, explained His blessing upon mankind so that they might infer from it His oneness, by saying, as a continuation of what preceded:

The discussion concerning the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[80] ﴿And Allah has made for you, from your houses, a place of rest; and He has made for you, from the hides of livestock, dwellings which you find light [to carry] on the day you travel and the day you camp; and from their wool, their fur, and their hair [He has made] household goods and provision for a time.﴾

﴿And Allah has made for you, from your houses, a place of rest﴾: that is, a place in which you dwell and to which you retreat, for countless aspects of your benefit. ﴿And He has made for you, from the hides of livestock, dwellings﴾: that is, other dwellings, namely tents, pavilions, and domes made from the hides themselves, or from the camel's hair, wool, and goat's hair as well. For insofar as they grow upon their hides, it is correct to say that they are from their hides; or "hides" is a metaphor for the whole. ﴿You find them light on the day of your travel and the day of your camping﴾: that is, you find them light to carry at the time of your departure and at the time of your alighting at your stopping places; their pitching does not burden you. Or they are light for you in the times of both travel and residence together. It has been said: the first is preferable, because the manifestation of the favour in their lightness is realized only in the state of travel, whereas for the one who settles, they are not burdensome.

﴿And from their wool, their fur, and their hair﴾: that is, and He has made for you from the wool of sheep, the fur of camels, and the hair of goats: ﴿household goods and provision for a time﴾. Al-athath (household goods) is what is made for use, whether for clothing or for spreading out. Al-mata' (provision) is what one acquires for trade. It has been said that both have the same meaning. The meaning of ﴿for a time﴾: that is, until you fulfill your needs from it, or until it wears out and perishes, or until you die.

Note:

The verse has been cited as evidence for the purity of the hides of edible animals, and of their wool, fur, and hair, whether they were taken while the animal was alive or after slaughter in the lawful manner (tadhkiyah).

And whoever permitted them absolutely, even from an animal not slaughtered in the lawful manner, has used the general wording of the verse as evidence. So it is stated in al-Iklil.

On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[81] ﴿And Allah has made for you, of what He has created, shades, and has made for you refuges among the mountains, and has made for you garments that protect you from the heat, and garments that protect you from your violence. Thus He completes His favor upon you, that perhaps you may submit.﴾

﴿And Allah has made for you, of what He has created﴾: i.e., of trees, mountains, buildings and other things. ﴿Shades﴾: i.e., shadows under which you shelter from the heat of the sun. ﴿And has made for you refuges among the mountains﴾: i.e., dwellings, strongholds and fortresses in which you take cover. ﴿And has made for you garments that protect you from the heat﴾: "garments" is the plural of sirbal (a garment), which means everything worn of cotton, wool and the like. He specified heat alone by mentioning one of the two opposites without the other. Or it is because protection from heat is more important to the Arabs, owing to its intensity in most of their lands, especially the inhabitants of the Hijaz, who are the primary audience of this address. It has been said that this is weakened by the earlier mention of protection from cold in His saying: ﴿For you therein is warmth﴾ [al-Nahl: 5]. This is the reason for restricting the mention to heat here, since its opposite has been mentioned earlier.

﴿And garments that protect you from your violence﴾: like coats of mail made of iron, chainmail (zarad) and the like, by which the enemy's weapons are warded off in war. ﴿Thus He completes His favor upon you, that perhaps you may submit﴾: i.e., so that you may reflect on the favors He has lavished upon you, the apparent and the hidden, the those within yourselves and those in the horizons, and thus submit your faces to Him, exalted is He, and believe in Him alone.

Abu al-Su'ud said: The singular "favor" (ni'mah) is either because what is meant is the verbal noun, or to show that this, in relation to the greatness of His side, is a small thing. It has been read "tasalamun" (تَسْلَمُونَ) with a fatha on the lam, meaning: from punishment or wounds.

The interpretation (ta'wil) of His saying, Exalted is He:

[82-84] ﴿But if they turn away, then upon you is only the clear notification.﴾ ﴿They recognize the favor of Allah; then they deny it, and most of them are disbelievers.﴾ [An-Nahl: 83] ﴿And [mention] the Day when We will raise up from every nation a witness; then permission will not be given to those who disbelieved, nor will they be asked to make amends.﴾ [An-Nahl: 84].

﴿But if they turn away﴾, i.e., after this clarification and this bestowal of blessings: ﴿then upon you is only the clear notification﴾.

﴿They recognize the favor of Allah﴾ [An-Nahl: 83], i.e., the favors that were enumerated, and that they come from His creation. ﴿Then they deny it﴾ [An-Nahl: 83], i.e., by worshipping other than the One who bestowed them, and by saying: they are from Allah, but through the intercession of our gods. ﴿And most of them are disbelievers﴾ [An-Nahl: 83].

(p-3846) Then Allah, Exalted is He, informed about their state in their return [to Him] by His saying:

﴿And [mention] the Day when We will raise up from every nation a witness﴾ [An-Nahl: 84], and he is its prophet, who will bear witness against it concerning what it answered him with of faith and disbelief regarding what had reached it. ﴿Then permission will not be given to those who disbelieved﴾ [An-Nahl: 84], i.e., to offer excuses, because they know its falsehood and lies, as in His saying: ﴿This is a Day when they will not speak﴾ [Al-Mursalat: 35], ﴿nor will they be permitted so that they could make excuses﴾ [Al-Mursalat: 36]. ﴿Nor will they be asked to make amends﴾ [An-Nahl: 84], i.e., they will not be asked for al-'utba (appeasement), meaning the removal of their Lord's displeasure and anger. (And al-'utba, with a ḍamma, is contentment, which is returning from wrongdoing to that which pleases the one who is displeased. It is said: istaʿtabahu, he gave him al-'utba by returning to his pleasure. And al-ʿatab is your blaming a man for an offense he committed against you, and a person only seeks ʿitāb (rebuke/reconciliation) from his opponent in order to remove what is in his heart against him of resentment and anger and return to being content with him. So when he does not seek ʿitāb from him, that indicates that he remains steadfast in his anger toward him.)

The interpretation (ta'wil) of His saying, Exalted is He:

[82-84] ﴿But if they turn away, then upon you is only the clear notification.﴾ ﴿They recognize the favor of Allah; then they deny it, and most of them are disbelievers.﴾ [An-Nahl: 83] ﴿And [mention] the Day when We will raise up from every nation a witness; then permission will not be given to those who disbelieved, nor will they be asked to make amends.﴾ [An-Nahl: 84].

﴿They recognize the favor of Allah﴾ [An-Nahl: 83], i.e., the favors that were enumerated, and that they come from His creation. ﴿Then they deny it﴾ [An-Nahl: 83], i.e., by worshipping other than the One who bestowed them, and by saying: they are from Allah, but through the intercession of our gods. ﴿And most of them are disbelievers﴾ [An-Nahl: 83].

(p-3846) Then Allah, Exalted is He, informed about their state in their return [to Him] by His saying:

﴿And [mention] the Day when We will raise up from every nation a witness﴾ [An-Nahl: 84], and he is its prophet, who will bear witness against it concerning what it answered him with of faith and disbelief regarding what had reached it. ﴿Then permission will not be given to those who disbelieved﴾ [An-Nahl: 84], i.e., to offer excuses, because they know its falsehood and lies, as in His saying: ﴿This is a Day when they will not speak﴾ [Al-Mursalat: 35], ﴿nor will they be permitted so that they could make excuses﴾ [Al-Mursalat: 36]. ﴿Nor will they be asked to make amends﴾ [An-Nahl: 84], i.e., they will not be asked for al-'utba (appeasement), meaning the removal of their Lord's displeasure and anger. It is said: istaʿtabahu, he gave him al-'utba by returning to his pleasure. And al-ʿatab is your blaming a man for an offense he committed against you, and a person only seeks ʿitāb (rebuke/reconciliation) from his opponent in order to remove what is in his heart against him of resentment and anger and return to being content with him. So when he does not seek ʿitāb from him, that indicates that he remains steadfast in his anger toward him.)

The interpretation (ta'wil) of His saying, Exalted is He:

[82-84] ﴿But if they turn away, then upon you is only the clear notification.﴾ ﴿They recognize the favor of Allah; then they deny it, and most of them are disbelievers.﴾ [An-Nahl: 83] ﴿And [mention] the Day when We will raise up from every nation a witness; then permission will not be given to those who disbelieved, nor will they be asked to make amends.﴾ [An-Nahl: 84].

﴿But if they turn away﴾, i.e., after this clarification and this bestowal of blessings: ﴿then upon you is only the clear notification﴾.

The Discussion on the Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[85-86] ﴿When those who did wrong see the punishment, it will not be lightened for them, nor will they be reprieved.﴾ ﴿When those who associated partners with God see their partners, they will say: "Our Lord, these are our partners whom we used to invoke besides You." But they will throw the word back at them: "Indeed, you are liars."﴾ [An-Nahl: 86].

﴿When those who did wrong see the punishment, it will not be lightened for them, nor will they be reprieved.﴾ That is: they will not be given respite (yu'akhkharun).

﴿When those who associated partners see their partners﴾ [An-Nahl: 86] meaning their idols which they worshipped: ﴿they will say: "Our Lord, these are our partners whom we used to invoke besides You"﴾ [An-Nahl: 86], that is, as lords, or whom we used to worship. ﴿But they will throw the word back at them: "Indeed, you are liars"﴾ [An-Nahl: 86]. That is: the idols answered them with denial of calling them partners and gods, glorifying God above association (tanzih). Or with denial of their claim that they had compelled them to worship them.

Abu Muslim al-Isfahani said: The intention of the polytheists is to shift this sin onto these idols, and they thought that this would save them from the punishment of God Exalted, or lessen their punishment. So at this point those idols deny them. This verse is like His saying: ﴿And who is more astray than one who calls upon other than God, one who will not respond to him until the Day of Resurrection, and they are unaware of their calling?﴾ [Al-Ahqaf: 5] ﴿And when mankind is gathered, they will be enemies to them and will deny their worship﴾ [Al-Ahqaf: 6]. And He Exalted said: ﴿And they have taken gods besides God that they might be for them a source of honor﴾ [Maryam: 81] ﴿No! They will deny their worship of them and will become opponents against them﴾ [Maryam: 82]. And His Exalted saying:

The commentary on His saying, exalted is He:

[87] ﴿And they will offer submission to Allah that Day, and what they used to fabricate will have strayed from them.﴾

﴿And they will offer﴾, i.e., those who wronged will offer ﴿submission to Allah that Day﴾, i.e., submission to His judgment, after their refusal in the world. ﴿And what they used to fabricate will have strayed from them﴾,

i.e., that Allah has partners and that they will intercede for them with Allah the Exalted. If it is asked: their denial has occurred, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿On the Day when Allah will resurrect them all and they will swear to Him as they swear to you﴾ [al-Mujadila: 18]. The answer (as al-Qashani said) is that this varies according to the stations (mawaqif). The denial occurs in the first station, at the time when the dispositions (hay'at) of vices are at their strongest, the soul's resolve in satanic conduct is at its firmest, and it is at the utmost distance from the Divine Light, being veiled by thick veils and dark coverings, so that it does not know that He sees it and observes it, and the lustre of the natural disposition (fitrah) is at its most clouded, so that it is able to display the opposite of what it requires. The submission occurs in the second station, after the passage of many long periods of the hours of the Day, whose measure is fifty thousand years, when the dispositions have dissipated and become tenuous, the soul's fibres have weakened in their vices, and it has drawn near the world of Light, because the veils have thinned and the light of its first natural disposition shines forth, so it acknowledges and submits. This is when the submission and denial pertain to particular souls. It may also be that submission occurs for some whose dispositions of vice have not become firmly rooted, whose veils have not grown thick, and whose light of readiness (isti'dad) has not been extinguished. [p-3848] Denial occurs for those in whom the dispositions have taken firm root and grown strong, in whom satanic nature has prevailed and become established, in whom the veil has become dense and readiness has been nullified. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 16, verses 88–89:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[88–89] ﴿Those who disbelieved and barred others from the way of Allah — We will increase them in punishment upon punishment for what they used to spread corruption.﴾ ﴿And the Day We raise up from every nation a witness against them from among themselves, and We bring you as a witness against these. And We have sent down to you the Book as an explanation of all things, and a guidance and mercy and good tidings for the Muslims.﴾ [al-Nahl: 89].

﴿Those who disbelieved and barred others from the way of Allah — We will increase them in punishment upon punishment for what they used to spread corruption.﴾ That is: He will multiply the punishment for them just as they multiplied their disbelief by barring others from faith. Like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and they forbid others from it and keep away from it themselves﴾ [al-An'am: 26]. In the verse there is evidence that the disbelievers differ in their punishment, just as believers differ in their ranks in Paradise and their degrees. As He, exalted is He, said: ﴿For each there is double, but you do not know﴾ [al-A'raf: 38].

﴿And the Day We raise up from every nation a witness against them from among themselves﴾ [al-Nahl: 89] — and this is their Prophet: ﴿and We bring you as a witness against these﴾ [al-Nahl: 89]. That is: remember that Day, and the great honour and lofty station that Allah bestowed upon you in it, and what the disbelievers will suffer in it of wishing that they were dust, due to the terror of the moment of appearance.

This has been mentioned in the verse of al-Nisa' in His saying: ﴿So how will it be when We bring from every nation a witness and bring you as a witness against these?﴾ [al-Nisa': 41] ﴿On that Day those who disbelieved and disobeyed the Messenger will wish that the earth were leveled over them, and they will not conceal from Allah a single statement﴾ [al-Nisa': 42]. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We have sent down to you the Book as an explanation of all things, and a guidance and mercy and good tidings for the Muslims﴾ [al-Nahl: 89] is a fresh (independent) statement, or a circumstantial clause with an implied (qad).

Al-Razi said: The connection of this statement to what precedes it is that when He, exalted is He, said: ﴿and We bring you as a witness against these﴾ [al-Nahl: 89], He made clear that He has removed their excuse regarding what they were obligated to. So they have no proof and no pretext.

Ibn Kathir said regarding this: The intended meaning, and Allah knows best, is that the One who imposed upon you the conveying of the Book He sent down to you will call you to account for that on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿Then We will surely question those to whom messengers were sent, and We will surely question the messengers﴾ [al-A'raf: 6]; ﴿So by your Lord, We will surely question them all﴾ [al-Hijr: 92]; ﴿about what they used to do﴾ [al-Hijr: 93]; ﴿The Day Allah will gather the messengers and say, "What was your response?" They will say, "We have no knowledge. Indeed, You are the Knower of the unseen."﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 109]. And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, He who has imposed upon you the Qur'an will surely return you to a place of return﴾ [al-Qasas: 85]; that is: The One who obligated you to convey the Qur'an will surely return you to Himself and restore you on the Day of Resurrection, and will call you to account for performing what He imposed upon you. This is one of the opinions, and it is a sound and good direction. End of quote.

And (al-tibyan) is among the verbal nouns formed on this pattern, to indicate the intensity and emphasis of the action. That is: an explanation of every beneficial knowledge — of the report of what came before, the knowledge of what will come, and every lawful and unlawful matter, and whatever people need in the affairs of their worldly life, their religion, their livelihood, and their return. ﴿And guidance﴾ [al-Nahl: 89] — that is, guidance for whoever submits and yields to the soundness of his nature toward its perfection. ﴿And mercy﴾ [al-Nahl: 89] — that is, for him, by conveying him to that perfection through upbringing and support, and his salvation from punishment, and good tidings to him of eternal happiness. And His saying, exalted is He:

(p-3850)

And His saying, exalted is He:

(p-3850)

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[90] ﴿Indeed, Allah orders justice and good conduct and giving to relatives, and forbids immorality and bad conduct and oppression. He admonishes you that you may be reminded.﴾

﴿Indeed, Allah orders﴾ — that is, in what He has sent down as an exposition of all things. ﴿Justice﴾ ('adl) is equity and evenhandedness in rights among you, abstaining from wrongdoing and giving each person with a right his right. ﴿Good conduct﴾ (ihsan) means excellence: that good is repaid with more than its like, and that evil is met with forgiveness. ﴿Giving to relatives﴾ means giving kinsfolk what they need. ﴿Forbids immorality﴾ means what is grossly shameful among sins and extreme in its ugliness, such as fornication. ﴿Bad conduct﴾ means everything the Sharia disapproves of. ﴿Oppression﴾ (baghy) means transgression against people. ﴿He admonishes you﴾ means He instructs you by what He commands and forbids you. ﴿That you may be reminded﴾ means that you may take heed of Allah's admonitions and act by what brings about Allah's pleasure, Exalted is He.

Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn Mas'ud: "The most comprehensive verse in the Qur'an, for good and for evil, is this verse."

Imam Ahmad narrated: "'Uthman ibn Maz'un passed by the Prophet (ﷺ) while he was sitting in the courtyard of his house, and 'Uthman looked at the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He said to him: 'Will you not sit?' He said: 'Yes.' So he sat. Then this verse was revealed to him, and he recited it to him. 'Uthman said: 'That was when faith settled in my heart and I loved Muhammad (ﷺ).'"

When this verse was recited to Aktham ibn Sayfi, he said to his people: "I see him commanding noble character and forbidding its opposite. So be leaders in this matter and do not be followers in it."

It is narrated from Ikrimah that "the Prophet (ﷺ) recited this verse to al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, and he said to him: 'O son of my brother! Repeat it for me,' so he repeated it. Al-Walid said: 'By Allah, it has sweetness, and it has radiance, its top is fruitful and its bottom is abundant, and it is not the speech of a human being.'"

It has been reported that the Banu Umayyah used to revile 'Ali, may Allah honour his face, in their sermons. When the caliphate came to 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz, may Allah be pleased with him, he removed that from them and established this verse in its place. It is among his greatest virtues.

Al-Nasir said: "Perhaps the reason this verse was substituted for those faults is that he noticed the correspondence between the mention of the prohibition of oppression (baghy) in it and the hadith transmitted that whoever opposed 'Ali is a rebel (baghi). For the Prophet (ﷺ) said to 'Ammar (who was of 'Ali's party): 'The rebellious group will kill you.' He was killed alongside 'Ali at the Battle of Siffin." End of quotation.

And also because of what it contains of justice and good conduct toward close relatives, and because it is the most comprehensive verse, as all that is mentioned in it is included. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 16, verse 91:

Then Allah the Exalted explained His command to fulfil the covenant and pact, and to observe oaths that have been confirmed, by His saying:

The discussion concerning the interpretation of the words of Allah the Exalted:

[91] ﴿And fulfil the covenant of Allah when you have taken it, and do not break oaths after their confirmation, while you have already made Allah your surety. Indeed, Allah knows what you do.﴾

﴿And fulfil the covenant of Allah when you have taken it, and do not break oaths after their confirmation, while you have already made Allah your surety. Indeed, Allah knows what you do.﴾

(p-3852) Ibn Jarir narrated "from Buraydah, who said: It was revealed concerning the pledge of allegiance to the Prophet (ﷺ). Whoever embraced Islam would pledge allegiance to the Prophet (ﷺ) upon Islam, and so they were commanded to fulfil this pledge and not to diminish it after its confirmation by oaths." That is: let not the scarcity of believers and the abundance of polytheists move you to break the pledge of allegiance you gave upon Islam. It is evident that the covenant (ʿahd) encompasses every matter whose fulfilment is obligatory by its requirement, of what a person binds himself to by his own choice, such as the pledge of allegiance upon Islam, the covenant of jihad, what he has bound himself to by a vow, and what he has confirmed by an oath. On this basis, the specific mention of the oath is to draw attention to the fact that it is the most important type of covenant for which care is obligatory. The words al-tawkid and al-ta'kid are two eloquent dialects (lughatan fasihatan); the original is the waw, and the hamza is a substitute for it. The waw in His saying: ﴿and you have already made Allah your surety﴾ is for the circumstantial clause (lil-hal) relating to the subject of ﴿break﴾, or to the subject of the verbal noun, even though it is elided. The meaning of ﴿kafil﴾ is a witness and an overseer. The word "making" (al-ja'l) is metaphorical, since whoever swears by Allah, the Exalted, while He is aware of it, is as though he has made Him a witness. Al-Shihab said: Had one kept "al-kafil" (surety) on its apparent sense, and taken it as an illustration of their not escaping His punishment, and that He will hand them over to it just as a surety hands over the one he has guaranteed, as one says: "Whoever wrongs has set up a surety for his wrong," as an alert that one cannot escape punishment, as al-Raghib mentioned, it would have been a highly eloquent meaning. His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah knows what you do﴾ is in the manner of an explanation of what precedes it, and in it is encouragement and warning.

Note:

The verse urges piety in oaths. It is clear that this applies to what involves obedience, righteousness and god-consciousness. As for other than that, the good lies in breaking it. This is indicated by what is established from the Prophet (ﷺ) in the Two Sahihs, that he said: "By Allah, if I swear an oath and then see something other than it to be better, I will do what is better and make expiation for my oath." In another narration: "and I expiated for my oath." Thus the hadith concerns one meaning, and the verse concerns another meaning. There is therefore no contradiction, as has been wrongly supposed. His saying, the Exalted:

(p-3853)

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[92] ﴿And do not be like her who unravels her spun thread after it has been made strong, into pieces. You take your oaths as a means of deceit among yourselves, lest one community be more numerous than another community. Allah only tests you thereby. And He will surely make clear to you on the Day of Resurrection that over which you used to differ.﴾

﴿And do not be like her who unravels her spun thread after it has been made strong, into pieces﴾ is an emphasis on the obligation of fulfilling oaths and the prohibition of breaking them. That is: do not be, in breaking your oaths, like the woman who unravels what she has spun, after she has made it firm and tightly twisted, turning it into pieces (ankath), that is, into fragments, out of her own folly and foolishness.

In the parable there is an indication that the one who breaks his oath is cast out of the ranks of complete men and enters the company of women. Indeed, he is among the lowest of them, namely the foolish one (al-kharqa').

His words, Exalted is He, ﴿You take your oaths as a means of deceit among yourselves﴾ are a circumstantial clause (hal) referring to the pronoun in "do not be." That is: do not be resembling a woman of such a condition, while you take your oaths as a corruption among yourselves. ﴿Lest one community be more numerous than another community﴾ means: because of a group, such as Quraysh, being greater in number and more abundant in wealth than a group such as the believers. ﴿Allah only tests you thereby﴾ means: He deals with you as one who tests you by their being more numerous, in order to see whether you will hold firmly to the rope of fulfilling the covenant of Allah and the oaths you have bound upon yourselves and strengthened in the pledge of allegiance to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), or whether you will be deceived by the multitude, wealth and power of Quraysh and by the fewness, poverty and weakness of the believers. ﴿And He will surely make clear to you on the Day of Resurrection that over which you used to differ﴾ means: then the truth will be distinguished from falsehood, by the degrees of reward and punishment that will become manifest. This is a warning and an admonition against opposing the religion of Islam.

Note:

Abu 'Ali al-Zajjaji, one of the imams of the Shafi'is, said: In this verse there is a foundation for what our companions say regarding the invalidity of circular reasoning (al-dawr), because Allah, Exalted is He, censured the one who returns to a thing by corrupting it after making it firm. He transmitted it in (al-Iklil).

(p-3854)

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[93] ﴿And if God had willed, He would have made you one community,﴾ that is, upright (ḥanīfa) and submitting (muslima). ﴿But He leads astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills, and you will surely be asked about what you used to do.﴾ That is, in this world, a questioning of rebuke and requital, not of inquiry and understanding. This is the kind of questioning that is negated in other than this verse, or it applies to one station rather than another, as has passed.

And His saying, exalted is He:

Commentary on the words of Allah, the Exalted:

[94] ﴿And do not take your oaths as means of deception between yourselves, lest a foot slip after its firmness and you taste evil for having averted [others] from the way of Allah; and for you there will be a great punishment.﴾

﴿And do not take your oaths as means of deception between yourselves﴾ is an explicit prohibition of it, after He had prohibited it implicitly, since He had taken it earlier as a restriction on what is forbidden. This is for emphasis upon them and to magnify the ugliness of what is forbidden. ﴿Lest a foot slip after its firmness﴾ means: lest your feet slip from the path of truth after they had become firmly established in it. ﴿And you taste evil﴾ means: that which will harm you in this world. ﴿For having averted [others]﴾ means: by your turning away from fulfilling [your oaths], or by your turning others away ﴿from the way of Allah﴾. ﴿And for you there will be a great punishment﴾ means: in the Hereafter.

A subtle point:

The indefinite form of (qadam, "foot") indicates that the slipping of a single foot is grave, so how much more so the slipping of many feet? Al-Bahr (al-Bahr al-Muhit, by Abu Hayyan) points to another nuance. He said: Plurality is sometimes regarded in terms of the group as a whole, so what belongs to it is given in the plural form. And sometimes each individual is regarded, so what belongs to it is given in the singular, as in His saying: ﴿And she prepared for them a banquet﴾ [Yusuf: 31], meaning: for each one of them a couch. Since the meaning is: none of you does this, the singular "qadam" was used in consideration of this meaning. Then He said: ﴿And you taste﴾ in consideration of the plural wording.

Al-Shihab (al-Khafaji) said: This is a justification of the singular from the standpoint of Arabic grammar, and it does not contradict the first nuance.

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[95] ﴿And do not trade the covenant of God for a small price. Indeed, what is with God is better for you, if you only knew.﴾

﴿And do not trade the covenant of God for a small price﴾ meaning: do not exchange the covenant of God and the pledge of allegiance to His Messenger for a fleeting, paltry worldly gain. This refers to what the Quraysh used to promise them and hold out as hopes, if they apostatized: ﴿Indeed, what is with God is better for you﴾, meaning: better than your prominence in this world and your reward in the Hereafter. ﴿If you only knew﴾, meaning: if you are among those possessing knowledge and discernment. And His, Exalted is He, saying:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[96] ﴿What you have with you will be exhausted, and what is with Allah is enduring. And We will surely give those who were patient their reward according to the best of what they used to do.﴾

﴿What you have with you will be exhausted, and what is with Allah is enduring﴾ is a justification for the superiority [of what is with Allah], by way of a resumptive statement (isti'naf). That is: what you have of that which you enjoy will run out and diminish, for it extends to a specified term, limited, determined, and finite. And what is with Him, exalted is He, of His reward for you in Paradise, is enduring, without cessation. For it is lasting, neither obstructed nor passing away. ﴿And We will surely give those who were patient their reward﴾, that is, for patience under the harm of the polytheists and the hardships of Islam, ﴿according to the best of what they used to do﴾, that is, with a recompense better than their deeds.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 16, verse 97:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[97] ﴿Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while he is a believer – We will surely cause him to live a good life, and We will surely reward them according to the best of what they used to do.﴾

﴿Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while he is a believer – We will surely cause him to live a good life, and We will surely reward them according to the best of what they used to do.﴾ This is a promise from Him, exalted is He, to whoever does righteousness – that is, the deed that follows the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger – whether male or female, and who remains firm upon his faith until death, that Allah, exalted is He, will cause him to live a good life.

Al-Mahayimi said: That is, he will take pleasure in his deed in this world more than the pleasure of the one who possesses wealth and status, and his pleasure is not nullified by his poverty, since Allah pleases him with His allotment, so He makes him content, and his concern for preserving and increasing wealth decreases. The disbeliever does not find his life pleasant through wealth and status, since he grows ever greedier and fearful of losing them. And they will be rewarded with the best in the Hereafter. So it will not be said to them: ﴿You used up your good things in your worldly life﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 20], but rather the lesser recompense of their deeds is completed in a manner that joins it to the higher. End of quotation.

In my view, the good life is the life in which there is the serenity of hearts through the pleasure of certainty, the sweetness of faith, the desire for what is promised, and contentment with the decree; and the freedom of the soul from that to which they were enslaved; and the tranquility in reliance upon one true Object of worship, and illumination by the secret of existence by which it subsists, and other of its virtues established in their proper places. This is in this world. As for the Hereafter, he has the best recompense and the fullest reward.

**On the interpretation of His saying (Exalted is He):**

[98–100] ﴿So when you recite the Qur'an, seek refuge in God from the accursed Satan.﴾ ﴿Indeed, he has no authority over those who believe and rely upon their Lord.﴾ [al-Nahl: 99] ﴿His authority is only over those who take him as an ally and those who associate others with Him.﴾ [al-Nahl: 100]

[p. 3857] ﴿So when you recite the Qur'an, seek refuge in God from the accursed Satan.﴾ ﴿Indeed, he has no authority over those who believe and rely upon their Lord.﴾ [al-Nahl: 99] ﴿His authority is only over those who take him as an ally and those who associate others with Him.﴾ [al-Nahl: 100]

Since the Qur'an is the Wise Reminder and the Clear Truth, and since every truth has an opponent, namely the devil of the jinn or of mankind, who stirs up doubts with his whisperings and corrupts hearts with his schemes, he (ﷺ) was commanded to seek refuge in God and take shelter with Him from his whispering when reciting the Qur'an, because human strength weakens in repelling it easily, so one needs to seek help against it from God and take refuge in His protection from it. The verse ﴿And We did not send before you any messenger or prophet but that when he spoke [or wished], Satan threw [something] into his wish. But God abolishes what Satan throws in. Then God makes His verses precise, and God is Knowing and Wise.﴾ [al-Hajj: 52] has shown that this is the habit of Satan following what every prophet recites to his nation of the renewed rulings revealed for the happiness of mankind: he diverts attention away from them and strives to demolish what was established for their sake. God makes His verses precise and abolishes the doubts of Satan, so that He may establish the truth and nullify falsehood. Since this was his habit, and it has its effect, there was a need to seek refuge in God from it when reciting the revelation and spreading its teachings.

Then God (Exalted is He) explained that the effect of his whispering occurs only on those over whom he has authority, that is, dominion and guardianship from his allies who follow his footsteps. As for those who believe and rely upon their Lord, who endure hardships and do not mind the stumbles they encounter in the path of jihad for the truth, he has no authority over them. They oppose his wishes and demolish everything he throws in, because their faith gives them the light that reveals his deceit, and their reliance upon God gives them strength through God, which prevents them from resisting Satan and from the power of his influence. The word (al-Rajim) (the accursed) is one of the dominant attributes of Satan, meaning: the cursed, the one stoned with curse, or the one driven away, or the one stoned with the stars. The pronoun in (bihi) refers to their Lord, and the (ba') is for transitivity (ta'diyah, i.e. making the verb transitive); or it refers to Satan, and the (ba') is causal, meaning: by means of him, his deception, and his whispering. This is preferred because the pronouns are unified in it. Some have pointed out that the meaning is: they associated him in the worship of God (Exalted is He), and all of this is what the noble wording allows and it is valid to intend it.

**Tanbih (a note):**

In the verse is the legislation of seeking refuge before recitation, and this includes the state of prayer and other times. A group held that it is obligatory, based on the apparent form of the command. Its wisdom, for other than the Prophet (ﷺ), is to seek protection with God so that Satan does not confuse the recitation and does not prevent reflection and remembrance.

The Commentary on the Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[101-102] ﴿And when We substitute one verse for another—and Allah knows best what He sends down—they say, "You are only a fabricator." But most of them do not know. Say, "The Holy Spirit has brought it down from your Lord in truth, to make firm those who believe, and as guidance and good tidings for the Muslims."﴾ [An-Nahl: 102].

﴿And when We substitute one verse for another—and Allah knows best what He sends down—they say, "You are only a fabricator." But most of them do not know. Say, "The Holy Spirit has brought it down from your Lord in truth, to make firm those who believe, and as guidance and good tidings for the Muslims."﴾ [An-Nahl: 102]

Al-tabdil (substitution) is the removal of a thing while placing something else in its position, so the substitution of a verse is its removal by another verse. The majority hold that the meaning is the abrogation (naskh, the replacement of a ruling or recitation by a later one) of a verse of the Qur'an, either in wording or in ruling, by another verse, for a profound wisdom alluded to in His words: ﴿and Allah knows best what He sends down﴾, namely, an abrogating verse which wisdom required that the earlier abrogated one be replaced by. Some people held that the meaning is the substitution of a sign from the earlier prophets, such as the signs of Moses, Jesus and others, which were cosmic and external, by another sign which is internal and cognitive, namely that what was sent down is guidance, mercy and glad tidings, which the intellect perceives when it reflects upon it and follows its natural order. This is because of the readiness of humanity at that time, since it addresses their intellect and calls upon their mouths and their minds. Thus they were not approached through cosmic marvels and dazzled by them, as had been the case with those who came before. So that was replaced by a sign which is the Book of knowledge and guidance from an unlettered Prophet who neither read nor wrote. And the Book's being clearly truthful, decisive in proof, and lucid in exposition is in relation to those who are given it and granted understanding. This second interpretation is preferred over the first, because the surah is Meccan, and there is no abrogation in a Meccan surah in the sense they intend. The detailed discussion belongs to another place, and we have alluded to this in two verses of Surat al-Baqarah, in His words: ﴿And if you are in doubt about what We have sent down﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 23], etc., and His words: ﴿Whatever verse We abrogate﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 106]. The point is that when He, Exalted is He, showed mercy to the worlds and made the Qur'an a substitute for what came before, they attributed what was revealed to Him to fabrication, rejecting the truth, opposing guidance, obeying Satan, and submitting to his whisperings. This was due only to their utmost ignorance, as He said: ﴿But most of them do not know.﴾ The parenthetical clause ﴿and Allah knows best what He sends down﴾ serves to rebuke the disbelievers and alert them to the corruption of their view.

Then He commanded him, Exalted is He, to declare the truth regarding it, saying: ﴿Say, "It has brought it down"﴾ [An-Nahl: 102], i.e., the Qur'an indicated by the verse. ﴿The Holy Spirit﴾ [An-Nahl: 102], meaning Jibril, peace be upon him. He is attributed to al-Qudus (holiness), which is purity, just as it is said: "Hatim al-Jud (Hatim of generosity), Zayd al-Khayr (Zayd of goodness), a bad news (khabar al-su'), and a truthful man (rajul sidq)." The intended meaning is: the holy spirit, the generous Hatim, the good Zayd, the bad news, and the truthful man. They attributed the described to the verbal noun of the attribute for emphasis on its frequent association with him and its exclusiveness to him. Al-muqaddas is what is purified from human impurities. The attribution of "the Lord" to his pronoun, blessings of Allah be upon him, in His words: ﴿from your Lord﴾ [An-Nahl: 102], is to indicate the establishment of the effusion of the effects of lordship. His words: ﴿in truth﴾ [An-Nahl: 102] mean: clothed with the established truth that accords with the wisdom required by the role of his era. His words, Exalted is He: ﴿to make firm those who believe﴾ [An-Nahl: 102] mean: upon the truth and rejecting the whisperings of the devils. In His words, Exalted is He: ﴿and as guidance and good tidings for the Muslims﴾ [An-Nahl: 102] there is an implicit allusion that the opposites of these qualities will occur for others.
