The discussion on the interpretation of His, exalted is He, saying:

[103] ﴿And We certainly know that they say, "Only a human is teaching him." The tongue of the one they refer to is foreign, while this is clear Arabic tongue.﴾

﴿And We certainly know that they say, "Only a human is teaching him." The tongue of the one they refer to is foreign, while this is clear Arabic tongue.﴾

He, exalted is He, informs about the polytheists, in their saying, other than the shameful statement that was reported from them earlier, and about their lying and slander, that the Messenger (ﷺ) is only being taught this (Qur'an) that he recites by a human. They meant a man who was a non-Arab (a'jami) living among them, who read the earlier scriptures, and perhaps the Prophet (ﷺ) would sometimes speak with him. He did not name him explicitly, to make clear that the root of their error does not lie in attributing to him, may the blessings of Allah be upon him, learning from a specific person, but rather from a human, whoever he might be. Then He, exalted is He, pointed out the clarity of the falsity of their slander, namely that the tongue of the man to whom they attribute the teaching is foreign and not clear. "And this noble Qur'an is a clear Arabic tongue," possessing clarity and eloquence (fasahah). And how could a non-Arab grasp the eloquence (balaghah) of this revelation and what it contains of sciences, let alone speak it, let alone be a teacher of it!

And His, exalted is He, saying:

The discussion of the words of God Most High:

[104–105] "Indeed, those who do not believe in the signs of Allah – Allah does not guide them, and for them is a painful punishment." "It is only those who do not believe in the signs of Allah who invent falsehood, and it is they who are the liars."

"Indeed, those who do not believe in the signs of Allah – Allah does not guide them, and for them is a painful punishment" is a warning to them for their disbelief in the Qur'an, after he (God) had removed their doubt and repelled their attack upon it.

As for His words, "It is only those who do not believe in the signs of Allah who invent falsehood" [16:105], it is a rejection of their saying, "You are only a fabricator" [16:101], and a reversal of the matter upon them, by clarifying that they are the fabricators, not he. The meaning is: inventing falsehood befits only one who is not believed, for he does not fear a punishment that would restrain him from it. As for His words, "And it is they who are the liars" [16:105], it refers to those who do not believe, and Quraysh enter among them as a primary entry. That is, they are the liars in reality and in fact; or, they are the most complete in it, for there is no greater lie than denying His signs and attacking them with such falsehoods. And there is no hiding what there is, after the restriction (qasr) of the restriction (hasr), of concern for his station, may the blessings of Allah be upon him. He was the most truthful, most righteous, and most complete of people in knowledge, action, faith and certainty, known for truthfulness among his people, such that none of them would doubt this, so much so that among them he was called by no name but "the Trustworthy Muhammad." For this reason, when Heraclius, king of the Romans, asked Abu Sufyan about those questions he asked concerning the attributes of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, among what he said to him was: "Did you accuse him of lying before he said what he said?" He said: "No." Heraclius said: "He would not leave off lying about people only to go and lie about Allah, Most High."

Note:

In this verse there is a strong indication that lying is among the greatest of major sins and the most vile of abominations. The proof of this is that the word "innama" (only) denotes restriction, and the meaning is that lying and fabrication are undertaken only by one who does not believe in the signs of Allah, and only by one who is a disbeliever. And this is, ultimately, a warning.

It is related that "the Prophet ﷺ was asked: Does the believer lie? He said: No. Then he recited this verse." Related by al-Razi.

And His words, Most High:

**The interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:**

[106–109] ﴿Whoever disbelieves in Allah after his belief—except one who is compelled while his heart is secure in faith—but those who open their breast to disbelief, upon them is wrath from Allah, and for them is a great punishment.﴾ ﴿That is because they preferred the worldly life over the Hereafter, and because Allah does not guide the disbelieving people.﴾ [An-Nahl: 107] ﴿Those are the ones whose hearts, hearing, and sight Allah has sealed, and they are the heedless.﴾ [An-Nahl: 108] ﴿Certainly, in the Hereafter they are the losers.﴾ [An-Nahl: 109]

When Allah, Exalted is He, had explained the virtue of those who believed and endured the harm of the polytheists in defending the religion, He followed it, through these verses, with the severe threat for apostasy and for preferring misguidance over guidance. He made an exception for the one who is compelled while his heart is secure in faith in Allah and His Messenger, for if he outwardly agrees with the polytheists in words, due to strong pain, severe harm, and threat of killing, then there is no blame upon him. The blame falls only upon one who opens his breast to disbelief, meaning he is content with it in himself and holds it as belief, preferring the transient worldly life, meaning choosing it over the lasting Hereafter. For such a person (p-3863) is the threat that the noble verses have explained: the wrath of Allah upon them first, His great punishment for them, which is the punishment of the Fire, second; the failure of their being guided, by their own choice of disbelief, third; fourth, the sealing upon their hearts through their hardness and their darkness, so that the path of understanding is not opened to them; and upon their hearing and sight, by blocking the path of the intended meaning from what they hear and the path of reflection from what they see, to the heart. Thus nothing of the means of guidance affects them, either through the inner path of the overflowing of knowledge and the shining of light, or through the outer path of teaching, learning, and reflection on the signs of Allah's creation. Fifth, they are truly the heedless, since they do not become alert in any way and their awakening from the sleep of ignorance is impossible for any reason. It is clear that each of these five calamities, taken individually, is among the greatest barriers to attaining good and happiness. How then when all of them are combined!

Al-Razi said: It is well known that man was placed in this world so that he would be like a merchant who buys the happiness of the Hereafter with his acts of obedience. When these obstacles occur, his loss becomes great. Therefore He said: ﴿Certainly, in the Hereafter they are the losers.﴾ [An-Nahl: 109], meaning: those whose worldly life is lost, the life for which they exhausted their strength in gaining, and in whose pursuit they wasted their lives, and they have nothing of the Hereafter except the consequence of regret.

**Notes:**

**First:** The *man* in His saying ﴿Whoever disbelieves﴾ is a relative pronoun serving as the subject (mubtada'), whose predicate is ﴿upon them is wrath﴾. His saying ﴿except one who is compelled﴾ is an exception placed before the ruling of wrath (istithna' muqaddam). His saying ﴿but those who open their breast﴾ returns to the beginning of the verse and its ruling, in a style that specifies and clarifies those who disbelieve, functioning as *'atf al-bayan* (explicative apposition) or *'atf al-tafsir* (explanatory apposition). I have not seen this grammatical analysis attributed to anyone, and it does not become apparent except to one who has tasted the sweetness of the Qur'an's style.

**Second:** The verse has been cited as evidence that the one compelled is not legally accountable, and that compulsion permits uttering a word of disbelief on condition that the heart remains secure in faith. The scholars also cited the verse as evidence for the invalidity of the divorce and manumission of one who is compelled, and of every statement or act issued by him, except what is excluded. This was reported by al-Suyuti in *al-Iklil*.

**Third:** It is related from Ibn 'Abbas that it was revealed concerning 'Ammar ibn Yasir, when the polytheists tortured him until he disbelieved in the Prophet (ﷺ), so he agreed with them under compulsion, and then came back apologizing. Ibn Jarir said: "The polytheists seized 'Ammar and tortured him until he nearly complied with some of what they wanted. He complained of that to the Prophet (ﷺ), who said to him: 'How do you find your heart?' He said: 'Secure in faith.' The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'If they return, then you return.'"

Ibn Ishaq said: The polytheists attacked those among his companions who had embraced Islam and followed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Every tribe rose against the Muslims among them, imprisoning them and torturing them with beating, hunger, and thirst, and by exposing them to the scorching sand of Makkah when the heat intensified, seeking to tempt them away from their religion. Some of them were tempted because of the severity of the trial that befell them, and some of them stood firm against them, and Allah protected them. Bilal, may Allah be pleased with him, was a slave of one of the Banu Jumah. Umayyah ibn Khalaf would bring him out when the midday heat grew intense, lay him on his back on the sand of Batha' in Makkah, then order a huge rock to be placed on his chest. Then he would say to him: "You will remain like this until you die or disbelieve in Muhammad and worship al-Lat and al-'Uzza." He would say, while in that trial: "One, One" (Ahad, Ahad), until Abu Bakr bought him and freed him.

The Banu Makhzum used to bring out 'Ammar ibn Yasir, his father, and his mother, may Allah be pleased with them, when the midday heat intensified, and torture them on the scorching sand of Makkah. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would pass by them and say: "Patience, family of Yasir, your promised place is Paradise." As for his mother, they killed her while she refused anything but Islam.

(p-3865) Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: I said to Ibn 'Abbas: "Did the polytheists inflict upon the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) torture to the extent that they would be excused for abandoning their religion?" He said: "Yes, by Allah! They would beat one of them, starve him, and deprive him of water, until he could not sit upright from the severity of the beating that had befallen him, until he gave them what they asked of him of disbelief, to the point that they would say to him: 'Are al-Lat and al-'Uzza your gods besides Allah?' and he would say: 'Yes.' To the point that a dung beetle would pass by them and they would say to him: 'Is this beetle your god besides Allah?' and he would say: 'Yes,' as a ransom from them, because of what they inflicted upon him of hardship."

Ibn Hisham mentioned in *al-Sirah* (The Biography), under the section (The Aggression of the Polytheists upon the Weak Among Those Who Embraced Islam, through Harm and Trial), strange reports on this subject, so consult it.

Ibn Kathir said: For this reason, the scholars agreed that one compelled to disbelieve may permissibly express outward compliance, to preserve his life. He may also permissibly refuse, as Bilal, may Allah be pleased with him, refused them while they inflicted terrible things upon him, and he kept saying: "One, One." And he said: "By Allah! If I knew a word that angers you more than this, I would say it!" May Allah be pleased with him and content him. Likewise Habib ibn Zayd al-Ansari, when Musaylimah the Liar said to him: "Do you testify that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah?" He would say: "Yes." He said: "Do you testify that I am the Messenger of Allah?" He would say: "I do not hear." So he kept cutting him into pieces, piece by piece, while he remained steadfast in that.

Al-Hafiz Ibn 'Asakir related, in the biography of 'Abdullah ibn Hudhafah al-Sahmi, one of the Companions, that the Romans captured him and brought him to their king. The king said to him: "Become a Christian, and I will make you a partner in my kingdom and marry you to my daughter." He said: "Even if you gave me all that you possess and all that the Arabs possess, on condition that I abandon the religion of Muhammad (ﷺ) for the blink of an eye, I would not do it." He said: "Then I will kill you." He said: "You and that." So he ordered him to be crucified, and ordered archers to shoot near his hands and feet, while he kept presenting to him the religion of Christianity and he refused. Then he ordered him to be taken down.

(p-3866) Then he ordered a cauldron to be heated, and a Muslim captive was brought and thrown into it while he watched, and his bones were seen glistening. He presented it to him again and he refused. So he ordered him to be thrown into it. He was lifted by the pulley to be cast into it, and he wept. The king desired him and called him, and he said: "I only wept because my soul is but one soul, which is about to be cast into this cauldron at this moment. I wished that I had as many souls as there are hairs on my body, each to be tortured in this manner for the sake of Allah."

In some reports: he imprisoned him and denied him food and drink for days. Then he sent him wine and pork, but he did not approach them. Then he summoned him and said: "What prevented you from eating?" He said: "As for it, it is permissible for me. But I did not want to give you cause to gloat over me." The king said to him: "Then kiss my head, and I will release you and release all the Muslim captives." He said: "So he kissed his head," and the king released with him all the Muslim captives who were with him. When he returned, 'Umar ibn al-Khattab said: "It is a right upon every Muslim to kiss the head of 'Abdullah ibn Hudhafah, and I will begin." So he stood and kissed his head.

And His saying, Exalted is He:

**The interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:**

[106–109] ﴿Whoever disbelieves in Allah after his belief—except one who is compelled while his heart is secure in faith—but those who open their breast to disbelief, upon them is wrath from Allah, and for them is a great punishment.﴾ ﴿That is because they preferred the worldly life over the Hereafter, and because Allah does not guide the disbelieving people.﴾ [An-Nahl: 107] ﴿Those are the ones whose hearts, hearing, and sight Allah has sealed, and they are the heedless.﴾ [An-Nahl: 108] ﴿Certainly, in the Hereafter they are the losers.﴾ [An-Nahl: 109]

﴿Whoever disbelieves in Allah after his belief—except one who is compelled while his heart is secure in faith—but those who open their breast to disbelief, upon them is wrath from Allah, and for them is a great punishment.﴾ ﴿That is because they preferred the worldly life over the Hereafter, and because Allah does not guide the disbelieving people.﴾ [An-Nahl: 107] ﴿Those are the ones whose hearts, hearing, and sight Allah has sealed, and they are the heedless.﴾ [An-Nahl: 108] ﴿Certainly, in the Hereafter they are the losers.﴾ [An-Nahl: 109]

When Allah, Exalted is He, had explained the virtue of those who believed and endured the harm of the polytheists in defending the religion, He followed it, through these verses, with the severe threat for apostasy and for preferring misguidance over guidance. He made an exception for the one who is compelled while his heart is secure in faith in Allah and His Messenger, for if he outwardly agrees with the polytheists in words, due to strong pain, severe harm, and threat of killing, then there is no blame upon him. The blame falls only upon one who opens his breast to disbelief, meaning he is content with it in himself and holds it as belief, preferring the transient worldly life, meaning choosing it over the lasting Hereafter. For such a person (p-3863) is the threat that the noble verses have explained: the wrath of Allah upon them first, His great punishment for them, which is the punishment of the Fire, second; the failure of their being guided, by their own choice of disbelief, third; fourth, the sealing upon their hearts through their hardness and their darkness, so that the path of understanding is not opened to them; and upon their hearing and sight, by blocking the path of the intended meaning from what they hear and the path of reflection from what they see, to the heart. Thus nothing of the means of guidance affects them, either through the inner path of the overflowing of knowledge and the shining of light, or through the outer path of teaching, learning, and reflection on the signs of Allah's creation. Fifth, they are truly the heedless, since they do not become alert in any way and their awakening from the sleep of ignorance is impossible for any reason. It is clear that each of these five calamities, taken individually, is among the greatest barriers to attaining good and happiness. How then when all of them are combined!

Al-Razi said: It is well known that man was placed in this world so that he would be like a merchant who buys the happiness of the Hereafter with his acts of obedience. When these obstacles occur, his loss becomes great. Therefore He said: ﴿Certainly, in the Hereafter they are the losers.﴾ [An-Nahl: 109], meaning: those whose worldly life is lost, the life for which they exhausted their strength in gaining, and in whose pursuit they wasted their lives, and they have nothing of the Hereafter except the consequence of regret.

**Notes:**

**First:** The *man* in His saying ﴿Whoever disbelieves﴾ is a relative pronoun serving as the subject (mubtada'), whose predicate is ﴿upon them is wrath﴾. His saying ﴿except one who is compelled﴾ is an exception placed before the ruling of wrath (istithna' muqaddam). His saying ﴿but those who open their breast﴾ returns to the beginning of the verse and its ruling, in a style that specifies and clarifies those who disbelieve, functioning as *'atf al-bayan* (explicative apposition) or *'atf al-tafsir* (explanatory apposition). I have not seen this grammatical analysis attributed to anyone, and it does not become apparent except to one who has tasted the sweetness of the Qur'an's style.

**Second:** The verse has been cited as evidence that the one compelled is not legally accountable, and that compulsion permits uttering a word of disbelief on condition that the heart remains secure in faith. The scholars also cited the verse as evidence for the invalidity of the divorce and manumission of one who is compelled, and of every statement or act issued by him, except what is excluded. This was reported by al-Suyuti in *al-Iklil*.

**Third:** It is related from Ibn 'Abbas that it was revealed concerning 'Ammar ibn Yasir, when the polytheists tortured him until he disbelieved in the Prophet (ﷺ), so he agreed with them under compulsion, and then came back apologizing. Ibn Jarir said: "The polytheists seized 'Ammar and tortured him until he nearly complied with some of what they wanted. He complained of that to the Prophet (ﷺ), who said to him: 'How do you find your heart?' He said: 'Secure in faith.' The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'If they return, then you return.'"

Ibn Ishaq said: The polytheists attacked those among his companions who had embraced Islam and followed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Every tribe rose against the Muslims among them, imprisoning them and torturing them with beating, hunger, and thirst, and by exposing them to the scorching sand of Makkah when the heat intensified, seeking to tempt them away from their religion. Some of them were tempted because of the severity of the trial that befell them, and some of them stood firm against them, and Allah protected them. Bilal, may Allah be pleased with him, was a slave of one of the Banu Jumah. Umayyah ibn Khalaf would bring him out when the midday heat grew intense, lay him on his back on the sand of Batha' in Makkah, then order a huge rock to be placed on his chest. Then he would say to him: "You will remain like this until you die or disbelieve in Muhammad and worship al-Lat and al-'Uzza." He would say, while in that trial: "One, One" (Ahad, Ahad), until Abu Bakr bought him and freed him.

The Banu Makhzum used to bring out 'Ammar ibn Yasir, his father, and his mother, may Allah be pleased with them, when the midday heat intensified, and torture them on the scorching sand of Makkah. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would pass by them and say: "Patience, family of Yasir, your promised place is Paradise." As for his mother, they killed her while she refused anything but Islam.

(p-3865) Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: I said to Ibn 'Abbas: "Did the polytheists inflict upon the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) torture to the extent that they would be excused for abandoning their religion?" He said: "Yes, by Allah! They would beat one of them, starve him, and deprive him of water, until he could not sit upright from the severity of the beating that had befallen him, until he gave them what they asked of him of disbelief, to the point that they would say to him: 'Are al-Lat and al-'Uzza your gods besides Allah?' and he would say: 'Yes.' To the point that a dung beetle would pass by them and they would say to him: 'Is this beetle your god besides Allah?' and he would say: 'Yes,' as a ransom from them, because of what they inflicted upon him of hardship."

Ibn Hisham mentioned in *al-Sirah* (The Biography), under the section (The Aggression of the Polytheists upon the Weak Among Those Who Embraced Islam, through Harm and Trial), strange reports on this subject, so consult it.

Ibn Kathir said: For this reason, the scholars agreed that one compelled to disbelieve may permissibly express outward compliance, to preserve his life. He may also permissibly refuse, as Bilal, may Allah be pleased with him, refused them while they inflicted terrible things upon him, and he kept saying: "One, One." And he said: "By Allah! If I knew a word that angers you more than this, I would say it!" May Allah be pleased with him and content him. Likewise Habib ibn Zayd al-Ansari, when Musaylimah the Liar said to him: "Do you testify that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah?" He would say: "Yes." He said: "Do you testify that I am the Messenger of Allah?" He would say: "I do not hear." So he kept cutting him into pieces, piece by piece, while he remained steadfast in that.

Al-Hafiz Ibn 'Asakir related, in the biography of 'Abdullah ibn Hudhafah al-Sahmi, one of the Companions, that the Romans captured him and brought him to their king. The king said to him: "Become a Christian, and I will make you a partner in my kingdom and marry you to my daughter." He said: "Even if you gave me all that you possess and all that the Arabs possess, on condition that I abandon the religion of Muhammad (ﷺ) for the blink of an eye, I would not do it." He said: "Then I will kill you." He said: "You and that." So he ordered him to be crucified, and ordered archers to shoot near his hands and feet, while he kept presenting to him the religion of Christianity and he refused. Then he ordered him to be taken down.

(p-3866) Then he ordered a cauldron to be heated, and a Muslim captive was brought and thrown into it while he watched, and his bones were seen glistening. He presented it to him again and he refused. So he ordered him to be thrown into it. He was lifted by the pulley to be cast into it, and he wept. The king desired him and called him, and he said: "I only wept because my soul is but one soul, which is about to be cast into this cauldron at this moment. I wished that I had as many souls as there are hairs on my body, each to be tortured in this manner for the sake of Allah."

In some reports: he imprisoned him and denied him food and drink for days. Then he sent him wine and pork, but he did not approach them. Then he summoned him and said: "What prevented you from eating?" He said: "As for it, it is permissible for me. But I did not want to give you cause to gloat over me." The king said to him: "Then kiss my head, and I will release you and release all the Muslim captives." He said: "So he kissed his head," and the king released with him all the Muslim captives who were with him. When he returned, 'Umar ibn al-Khattab said: "It is a right upon every Muslim to kiss the head of 'Abdullah ibn Hudhafah, and I will begin." So he stood and kissed his head.

And His saying, Exalted is He:

The discussion on the interpretation of His, the Exalted, statement:

[110] ﴿Then indeed your Lord – for those who emigrated after they had been tried, then struggled and were patient – indeed your Lord, after that, is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.﴾.

﴿Then indeed your Lord – for those who emigrated after they had been tried, then struggled and were patient – indeed your Lord, after that, is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.﴾ is an explanation concerning those who were oppressed in Makkah and humiliated among their people, and who outwardly agreed with them in the trial. Then Allah made deliverance possible for them through emigration (hijrah), so they abandoned their lands, their families and their wealth, seeking the good pleasure of Allah and His forgiveness, and they struggled against the disbelievers and were patient through the hardships of striving. He, the Exalted, informed that these people, after the aforementioned trial, meaning their having complied with it: ﴿Most Forgiving, Most Merciful﴾. So He forgives them what has passed from them, and shows them mercy through the good reward.

The preposition (al-jarr) in His statement ﴿for those﴾ is connected to the predicate (al-khabar, the predicate of the sentence) by way of inversion of its order, and the predicate belongs to the first (inna, the emphatic particle). The second ﴿inna﴾ is repeated for emphasis. Or it belongs to the second, and the predicate of the first is implied. His statement ﴿emigrated﴾ included those who emigrated from Makkah to Abyssinia, fleeing with their religion from the trial, and those who afterwards emigrated to Madinah in the same manner. It also included His statement ﴿struggled﴾ in spreading the truth, propagating the word of faith and defending it. Or it means they fought in the way of Allah. Because of this possibility in the two verbs, it has been said that the verse is Madani, and His, the Exalted, statement:

**Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 16, verse 111:**

The discussion of the explanation (*ta'wil*, interpretation) of His saying, may He be exalted:

[111] ﴿On the Day when every soul comes pleading for itself, and every soul will be paid in full for what it did, and they will not be wronged.﴾

﴿On the Day when every soul comes pleading for itself﴾ is in the accusative case, governed either by ﴿رَحِيمٌ﴾ or by ﴿اذْكُرْ﴾ (remember). The Day is the Day of Resurrection. The meaning of ﴿تُجادِلُ﴾ is: it argues on its own behalf and strives for its own deliverance. It is concerned with nothing but itself and its own condition. Neither wealth, nor father, nor son, nor anything at all will avail it. ﴿And every soul will be paid in full for what it did﴾, that is, for good and evil. ﴿And they will not be wronged﴾ in that. Then He, exalted is He, says:

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 16, verses 112–113:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[112–113] ﴿And Allah presents an example: a city that was secure and tranquil, its provision coming to it abundantly from every place. But it denied the favors of Allah, so Allah made it taste the garment of hunger and fear for what they used to do.﴾ ﴿And there had certainly come to them a messenger from among themselves, but they denied him, so the punishment seized them while they were wrongdoers.﴾ [An-Nahl: 113].

﴿And Allah presents an example: a city that was secure and tranquil, its provision coming to it abundantly from every place. But it denied the favors of Allah, so Allah made it taste the garment of hunger and fear for what they used to do.﴾ ﴿And there had certainly come to them a messenger from among themselves, but they denied him, so the punishment seized them while they were wrongdoers.﴾ [An-Nahl: 113]

Know that when He threatened the disbelievers with a severe warning in the Hereafter, He also warned them of His vengeance in this world, through hunger and fear. The meaning of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And Allah presents an example: a city﴾ is: He made the city whose condition is this an example for every people upon whom Allah has bestowed favors. Then the blessing made them insolent, so they disbelieved and turned away, and Allah sent down His vengeance upon them. Thus the people of Mecca enter into this primarily, or it refers to specific people, namely the people of Mecca. The "city" is either understood as hypothetical, described with this attribute and not specific, since the existence of the comparison does not necessarily require the existence of what is compared; or it is specific, one of the cities of the earlier peoples. The verb (ḍaraba, "presents") is construed with the meaning of (ja'ala, "made"), with (mathalan, "an example") as the second object and (qaryatan, "a city") as the first object.

Abu al-Su'ud said: The placement of (qaryatan, "a city") after the second object, though it is the first object, is so that the second object does not come between it and its description and what follows from it; for delaying it from the whole would disrupt the interlinking of the parts of the composition and its harmony. Also, delaying what by right should be placed first produces in the soul an expectation for its arrival and a longing for it, especially when the preceding part contains what calls to it. For the example calls for preserving the details of the condition of that which is the example, so that the delayed element, when it arrives, settles there with greater firmness. The word "city" is meant figuratively as its people, or by way of an implied modifier. The meaning of its being: ﴿secure and tranquil﴾ is that no fear disturbs it. (Ar-Raghad, "abundantly") means wide and ample. (Al-An'um) is the plural of (ni'mah, "favor").

In His saying: ﴿So Allah made it taste the garment of hunger and fear﴾, the effect of hunger and fear and their harm encompassing them is likened to a garment covering the one who wears it. So its name is borrowed for it, and the borrowed verb "make taste" is applied to it for the general sense of reaching, which indicates the intensity of the affliction, including what it contains of the combined perceptions of touch and taste, in the manner of abstraction. For, due to the widespread use of this expression and its frequent occurrence on tongues, it has taken on the status of a literal usage.

Ibn Kathir said: This is an example meant to refer to the people of Mecca. For it was secure, tranquil and settled, people were snatched away from around it, and whoever entered it was safe and did not fear, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And they said, "If we follow the guidance with you, we will be snatched away from our land." Have We not established for them a secure sanctuary to which the fruits of every thing are brought as provision from Us?﴾ [Al-Qasas: 57]. Likewise He said here: ﴿its provision coming to it abundantly﴾, meaning easily and comfortably: ﴿from every place﴾. ﴿But it denied the favors of Allah﴾, meaning it rejected the bounties of Allah upon it, the greatest of which was the sending of Muhammad ﷺ to them, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Have you not seen those who exchanged the favor of Allah for disbelief and caused their people to settle in the abode of ruin? Hell, they will burn therein, and wretched is the settlement﴾ [Ibrahim: 28–29]. Therefore Allah replaced their former two states with their opposites, and said: ﴿So Allah made it taste the garment of hunger and fear﴾, meaning He clothed it with and made it taste hunger after what had been brought to them, the fruits of every thing, and its provision had come to it from every place. That was because they disobeyed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and refused except to oppose him, so he invoked against them with seven years like the seven years of Joseph. A year struck them that took away everything they had, so they ate al-'ilhiz (he said: it is camel's hair mixed with its blood when it is slaughtered). And His saying: ﴿and fear﴾: that is because they exchanged their security for fear of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his companions when they emigrated to Medina, from his might and his raiding parties and armies, and he reduced all they had to ruin and degradation, until Allah granted it to them as conquest. That was due to their own doing, their transgression and their denial of the Messenger ﷺ whom Allah sent among them, from among themselves. He bestowed this as a favor upon them in His saying: ﴿Certainly did Allah confer favor upon the believers when He sent among them a messenger from among themselves﴾ [Al 'Imran: 164], and the verse. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So fear Allah, O men of understanding who have believed. Allah has certainly sent down to you a reminder﴾ [At-Talaq: 10] ﴿a messenger﴾ [At-Talaq: 11], and His saying: ﴿As We have sent among you a messenger from among yourselves, reciting to you Our verses and purifying you and teaching you the Book and wisdom﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 151] up to His saying: ﴿and do not deny Me﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 152]. And just as their condition was reversed upon the disbelievers, so that they feared after security and went hungry after abundance, Allah replaced the believers' fear with security, provided for them after poverty, and made them leaders of the people, their rulers, masters, commanders and imams. End.

(p-3870) Then Allah, exalted is He, exposed the error of the polytheists in forbidding what Allah had made lawful, such as the baheera, the saiba and others, detailing what He had forbidden, of that which is not in it, which they used to forbid by their own whims. And it is permitted to eat it, as He said:

The discussion concerning the interpretation of His, exalted is He, saying:

[114] ﴿So eat of what Allah has provided for you, lawful and good, and be grateful for the favor of Allah, if it is Him that you worship.﴾

﴿So eat of what Allah has provided for you﴾, i.e., of the tilth (ḥarth) and the cattle (an'ām): ﴿lawful and good. And be grateful for the favor of Allah, if it is Him that you worship﴾, i.e., if you intend to worship Him, then make lawful what they (He) has made lawful, for worshipping Him lies in declaring them lawful. And be grateful to Him, for He alone is the Bestower of this bounty and the Gracious One in it.

Then He mentioned what He forbade them, of that which contains harm to them in their religion and their worldly life, by His saying:

The discussion of the interpretation of His statement, exalted is He:

[115] ﴿Indeed, He has forbidden you only carrion, blood, the flesh of swine, and that which has been dedicated to other than Allah. But whoever is compelled [by necessity], neither desiring [it] nor exceeding [the limit], then indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

﴿Indeed, He has forbidden you only carrion, blood, the flesh of swine, and that which has been dedicated to other than Allah⁠—﴾ i.e., slaughtered in the name of other than Him, exalted is He. ﴿But whoever is compelled﴾ i.e., driven by hardship to what Allah has forbidden, ﴿neither desiring [it] nor exceeding [the limit]﴾ i.e., transgressing beyond the measure of necessity and the staving off of hunger. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ i.e., He will not hold him accountable for that.

The discussion of a verse like this has already preceded in Surat al-Baqarah with what is sufficient, so there is no need to repeat it.

Then, exalted is He forbade following the way of the polytheists, who made lawful and unlawful by the mere descriptions and names they devised and agreed upon according to their own opinions, such as the baḥīrah, the sā'ibah, the waṣīlah, the ḥām, and others, which were a law they had innovated in their pre-Islamic ignorance (jāhiliyyah). So He said:

(p-3871)

The discussion of the words of Allah the Exalted:

[116-117] ﴿And do not say, concerning what your tongues describe falsely, "This is lawful and this is unlawful," to invent lies against Allah. Indeed, those who invent lies against Allah will not succeed. A brief enjoyment, and for them is a painful punishment.﴾ [al-Nahl: 117].

﴿And do not say, concerning what your tongues describe falsely, "This is lawful and this is unlawful," to invent lies against Allah. Indeed, those who invent lies against Allah will not succeed. A brief enjoyment, and for them is a painful punishment.﴾ [al-Nahl: 117]

That is: do not say the lie concerning what your tongues describe of the livestock as lawful or unlawful, in your saying: ﴿That which is in the wombs of these cattle is exclusively for our males and forbidden to our wives﴾ [al-An'am: 139], without that description being grounded in revelation from Allah. So (al-kadhib, "the lie") is the object of (taqulu, "say"), and His saying ﴿This is lawful and this is unlawful﴾ is an apposition (badal) to (al-kadhib). The lam is attached to the saying (lil-qawl), as one says: "Do not say of nabidh (date wine) that it is lawful," meaning: concerning its matter and its right. So it denotes specification (lil-ikhtisas). In this is an indication that it is merely a statement by the tongue, not a firmly established ruling.

Or: ﴿This is lawful﴾ is the object of (taqulu), and (al-kadhib) is the object of (tasif, "describe"), and the lam in ﴿concerning what your tongues describe﴾ is causal (ta'lilliyya), and (ma) is verbal-masdarial (masdariyya). The meaning of (tasif) is "mention." His saying ﴿to invent lies﴾ is an apposition to the first causal clause. That is: do not say "This is lawful and this is unlawful" because of your tongues describing a lie, i.e., because of a statement your tongues utter without any proof. It is not a repetition of His saying ﴿to invent lies against Allah﴾, because this affirms lying in absolute terms, whereas that affirms lying against Allah. It indicates that they, through their habituation to lying, grew bold in lying against Allah, so they attributed to Him what they had made lawful and unlawful.

On this reading, where (al-kadhib) is the object of (tasif), there is an exaggeration in describing their tongues as describing lying, by making it the very essence of lying, rising beyond it to the point that it is imagined that the reality of lying was unknown until their speech revealed and clarified the reality of lying. So (tasif) means "clarify." It is thus like a definition and description that unveils the reality of lying. The definite article in (al-kadhib) is for the genus. As if their tongues, when they speak, uncover its truth. Upon this is the saying of al-Ma'arri:

"The lightning of al-Ma'arra passed after weakness, so it spent the night at Barrama describing the weariness."

Similar is: "His day is fasting," when the day is described with what is described of a person, because that action occurs in it frequently. And "Her face describes beauty," because her face, being described with surpassing beauty, became as if it were the reality of beauty and its source, from which it is known, so that it is as if it describes and defines it, like his saying:

"Your hand has become fashioned from generosity, nay, rather your hand has been fashioned from it, and generosity was formed."

This is metaphorical attribution (al-isnad al-majazi). Or we may say: her face describes beauty through the tongue of the state (lisan al-hal), so it is a implicit metaphor (isti'ara makniyya), as if it says: "Nothing of me is but beauty itself." Its like occurs in the speech of the Arabs and non-Arabs. This is the essence of what is in the commentaries on the Kashshaf.

What is in the verse is more eloquent than the cited example, for the reasons you have heard. This is what "al-'Inaya" conveyed. The lam in ﴿to invent﴾ is the lam of outcome and consequence (lam al-sayrura wal-'aqiba), borrowed from the causal sense, since what proceeded from them was not for this purpose, but for other aims, upon which what was mentioned follows. It is permitted that it be causal, and their intent for that is not remote. In His saying ﴿Indeed, those who invent lies﴾ up to the end of the verse, there is a severe warning that they will not attain success or achieve any sought goal that is valued, neither in this world nor in the Hereafter. As for this world, what they invent lies for is a brief enjoyment that soon ends. As for the Hereafter, ﴿for them is a painful punishment﴾, as He said: ﴿We grant them enjoyment briefly, then We will compel them to a harsh punishment﴾ [Luqman: 24].

Note:

Al-Hafiz Ibn Kathir said: Included in the verse is everyone who innovates an innovation for which he has no legislative basis, or who makes lawful something Allah has forbidden, or forbids something Allah has permitted, by his mere opinion and whim.

﴿And do not say, concerning what your tongues describe falsely, "This is lawful and this is unlawful," to invent lies against Allah. Indeed, those who invent lies against Allah will not succeed. A brief enjoyment, and for them is a painful punishment.﴾ [al-Nahl: 117]

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 16, verses 118–119:

The discussion of His saying, may He be exalted:

[118–119] ﴿And to those who were Jews We prohibited what We have related to you before. And We did not wrong them, but they were wronging themselves.﴾ ﴿Then indeed, your Lord – for those who did evil in ignorance and then repented after that and corrected themselves – indeed, your Lord, after that, is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ [al-Nahl: 119].

﴿And to those who were Jews﴾ means the Jews. ﴿We prohibited what We have related to you before﴾ i.e. (p-3874) in Surat al-An'am, in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And to those who were Jews We prohibited every animal with claws. And of cattle and sheep We prohibited to them their fat, except what their backs carry or the intestines or what is mixed with bone. That We recompensed them for their rebellion. And indeed, We are truthful.﴾ [al-An'am: 146], the verse. ﴿And We did not wrong them﴾ i.e. in what We prohibited for them. ﴿But they were wronging themselves﴾ i.e. they deserved that. Like His saying: ﴿For wrongdoing from those who were Jews, We made unlawful for them good things which had been lawful for them and for their hindering from the way of Allah many times over.﴾ [al-Nisa: 160]. What they mentioned in its interpretation that could come here has already passed for us, so recall it. They said: In the verse there is an indication of the difference between them and others regarding prohibition. For this nation was not prohibited anything except what contains harm for it. And others may be prohibited what has no harm in it, as a punishment for them through deprivation, like the Jews.

Then He, may He be exalted, explained the great magnitude of His grace in accepting the repentance of whoever among the disobedient repents, by His saying:

﴿Then indeed, your Lord – for those who did evil in ignorance and then repented after that and corrected themselves – indeed, your Lord, after that, is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ [al-Nahl: 119] i.e. the action between them and their Lord; ﴿indeed, your Lord, after it﴾ [al-Nahl: 119] i.e. the repentance; ﴿is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Nahl: 119].

Then He, may He be exalted, praised Ibrahim, peace be upon him, calling them to follow his way in monotheism and rejecting idolatry, and clearing his station of what they were slandering him with, by His saying, glorified is He:

The discussion concerning the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[120-121] ﴿Indeed, Abraham was a nation, devoutly obedient to Allah, inclining toward truth, and he was not of those who associate others with Allah.﴾ ﴿Grateful for His favors. He chose him and guided him to a straight path.﴾ [al-Nahl: 121].

﴿Indeed, Abraham was a nation﴾, i.e., a leader who is to be followed, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, I will make you a leader for the people﴾ [al-Baqarah: 124]. Or, he alone was a nation among the nations, because he combined perfections not found in anyone else. ﴿Devoutly obedient to Allah﴾, i.e., humbly submissive to Him, standing by what He commanded. ﴿Inclining toward truth﴾, i.e., turning away from every false religion toward the true religion. ﴿And he was not of those who associate others with Allah.﴾ ﴿Grateful for His favors﴾ [al-Nahl: 121], i.e., attending to the thanks for the blessings of Allah upon him, using them in the manner that is proper, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And Abraham, who fulfilled [his commitments]﴾ [al-Najm: 37], i.e., he carried out everything Allah, exalted is He, had commanded him. ﴿He chose him﴾ [al-Nahl: 121], i.e., He selected him and chose him for prophethood. ﴿And guided him to a straight path﴾ [al-Nahl: 121], which is the worship of Allah alone, without partner, according to an approved law.

The discourse on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[122-123] "And We gave him in this world good, and indeed he is in the Hereafter among the righteous. Then We revealed to you, [O Muhammad], that you follow the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth, and he was not of those who associate others with Allah." [An-Nahl: 123].

"And We gave him in this world good" — i.e., of the good mention (al-dhikr al-jamil), as He said: "And We granted them a tongue of truthfulness and high station" [Maryam: 50], and of the blessing and peace upon him, as He said: "And We left for him among later generations [the salutation]" [As-Saffat: 108], "Peace upon Abraham" [As-Saffat: 109], and of His providing him with enjoyments of worldly portions so that he would be strengthened to carry out the rights of servanthood. "And indeed he is in the Hereafter" — i.e., in the world of spirits — "among the righteous" — i.e., those firmly established in the station of uprightness, by rendering to every possessor of a right his right, those who have the highest ranks in Paradise.

"Then We revealed to you, [O Muhammad], that you follow the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth, and he was not of those who associate others with Allah" [An-Nahl: 123] — i.e., after these honours and good things which We gave him in both abodes, We honoured and ennobled him by Our command, by your following him in monotheism and the fundamental principles of religion which do not change across the revealed laws, such as the matter of the origin, the return, the gathering and the recompense, and the like, not in the branches of the Shariah, its particular forms and its rulings, for these change according to the interests and the differences of times and natures, and what people's conditions have of customs and dispositions. Thus said al-Qashani.

In (al-Iklil): Our companions (the Shafi'is) took as evidence this verse for the obligation of circumcision, and whatever was of his law, and no abrogating text has come concerning it.

(p-3876) A subtle point:

Al-Zamakhshari said: In "{thumma}" [then] here is what it contains of magnifying the station of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and exalting his rank, and an indication that the most noble of what the Friend of Allah, Ibrahim ﷺ, was granted of honour and the most sublime of the blessings bestowed upon him was that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ follows his religion, because it indicates the great distance of this attribute in rank among the rest of the attributes with which Allah praised him.

Al-Nasir said: The reason "thumma" conveys this is that it is in its original usage for the delay of the conjoined element in time; then it was used for its delay from it in elevation of rank, such that the conjoined element is loftier in station than that to which it is conjoined. So it is as if, after enumerating the virtues of the Friend, peace be upon him, He said, exalted is He, and here is what is higher than all of that in worth, loftier in rank, and more exalted in eminence, namely that the Prophet ﷺ, the unlettered one, who is the master of mankind, follows the religion of Abraham, and is commanded by revelation to follow it, his command in this being recited in the Mighty Qur'an. In this there is magnification of both of them together. But the Prophet's ﷺ share of this magnification is fuller and greater, as we have laid out. And His words, exalted is He:

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 16, verse 124:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[124] ﴿The Sabbath was only enjoined upon those who differed concerning it. And indeed, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that wherein they used to differ.﴾

﴿The Sabbath was only enjoined upon those who differed concerning it﴾ meaning the Jews. He made it obligatory upon them to sanctify it and to rest themselves and their animals from work on it. But they transgressed concerning it and resorted to tricks to make it lawful.

Al-Qashani said: That is, what was not imposed upon you; it was only imposed upon them. So it does not oblige you to follow Musa in that, but rather to follow Ibrahim. As for His saying, exalted is He, ﴿And indeed, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that wherein they used to differ﴾, that is, by requiting them for their differing, meaning their corruption and their deviation from the path of truth.

Then Allah the Exalted explained the etiquette of calling to His true religion, with His words:

The discussion on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[125] ﴿Invite to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good admonition, and argue with them in the best manner. Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has strayed from His way, and He is most knowing of those who are guided.﴾

﴿Invite to the way of your Lord with wisdom﴾ i.e., with a sound, firm statement, which is the proof that clarifies the truth and removes doubt. ﴿And good admonition﴾ i.e., gentle lessons and frightening events, so that they may beware of His punishment. ﴿And argue with them in the best manner﴾ i.e., argue with those who oppose you by the manner that is the best of the ways of disputation, through gentleness, softness, and good speech, without harshness, for that is more effective in quelling their flame. And His words, exalted is He, ﴿Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has strayed from His way, and He is most knowing of those who are guided﴾ mean: upon you is only the conveying and the calling in the described manner, so do not let your soul go to waste in sorrow over those among them who have strayed, for it is not upon you to guide them; for He is most knowing of who will remain in error and who will be guided to it, and He will recompense each of the two with what it deserves. Or the meaning is: follow in calling and debating the method mentioned. For Allah the Exalted is most knowing of the state of one who does not refrain from error according to the requirement of his acquired disposition, and of the state of one whose affair will lead to guidance because of the natural good within him. So what He has prescribed for you in calling is what wisdom requires, for it is sufficient for guiding those who are guided and for removing the excuse of those who go astray. This was related from Abu al-Su'ud.

Caution:

His words, exalted is He, ﴿and argue with them in the best manner﴾ indicate the exhortation to fairness in debate, to following the truth, and to gentleness and forbearance, in a way that makes clear that the aim is to establish the truth and nullify falsehood, and that there is no purpose other than this.

And His words, exalted is He:

(p-3878)

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying:

[126] ﴿And if you punish, then punish with the like of that with which you were punished. But if you are patient, it is indeed better for the patient.﴾.

﴿And if you punish, then punish with the like of that with which you were punished. But if you are patient, it is indeed better for the patient.﴾ That is: hold to the way of justice ('adala) and do not go beyond it, for it is the lowest level of your perfection. If you have a foothold in chivalry (futuwwa) and a firmly rooted vein of virtue, generosity and manliness, then leave off seeking victory and revenge against the one who wronged you. Meet him with pardon while you have the power, and be patient over the offence, for ﴿it is indeed better for the patient﴾. Do you not see how He emphasized it with the oath and the lam in its answer, and how He moved from the pronoun to the noun, so that instead of saying (لَهو خَيْرٌ لَكم) ("it is better for you"), He said ﴿it is indeed better for the patient﴾? This is to record praise and exaltation upon them through the attribute of patience. The patient one has risen above the station of the lower self (nafs) and has met the action of his companion's lower self with the attribute of the heart. So he is not troubled by the appearance of the attribute of the lower self, and he opposes the darkness of his companion's lower self with the light of his heart. Often he repents and passes over the station of the lower self, and the fury of his anger is broken, so he becomes righteous. But if you do not have this noble station, then do not punish the wrongdoer with the surge of anger beyond what he has done to you, lest you commit injustice, or fall into the most vile and foul vices, so that your state is corrupted and your burden grows heavier than the burden of the offender. This was related by al-Qashani.

Notes:

The first: In al-Iklil, Ibn al-'Arabi said: The verse permits equivalence in retaliation (qisas), contrary to those who said: there is no retaliation except by the sword. It is also cited for the issue of taking back one's right, as Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Ibn Sirin and al-Nakha'i that the two of them used it as evidence for it. The wording of al-Nakha'i: He was asked about a man who betrays another man, and then the man comes into possession of dirhams belonging to him? He said: If he wishes, he may take from his dirhams the equivalent of what he betrayed him with. Then he recited this verse. The wording of Ibn Sirin: If a man takes something from you, then take the like of it.

(p-3879) Ibn Kathir said: So also said Mujahid, Ibrahim, al-Hasan al-Basri and others, and Ibn Jarir chose it. Its generality therefore includes justice in retaliation and equivalence in exacting one's right.

The second: Muhammad ibn Ishaq related from some of his companions, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, who said: The whole of Surat al-Nahl was revealed at Makka, and it is Makki except for the last three verses, which were revealed at Madina after Uhud, when Hamza (may Allah be pleased with him) was killed and mutilated. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If Allah grants me victory over them, I will mutilate thirty men of them." When the Muslims heard that, they said: "By Allah, if Allah grants us victory over them, we will mutilate them with a mutilation that no one of the Arabs has inflicted upon anyone ever." So Allah revealed this verse, to the end of the surah.

The Hafiz Ibn Kathir said: This is mursal (a report lacking a companion in its chain), and in it is an unnamed person. The Hafiz al-Bazzar related it through another route, connected, from Abu Hurayra (may Allah be pleased with him): that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood over Hamza ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib (may Allah be pleased with him) when he was martyred, and he looked upon a sight more painful to the heart than it, for he had been mutilated. He said: "May the mercy of Allah be upon you. You were, as far as I knew, one who kept the ties of kinship and did much good. By Allah, were it not for the grief of those after you over you, I would have been pleased to leave you until Allah raises you from the bellies of beasts of prey (or a word like it). Indeed, by Allah, for that I will mutilate seventy men like your mutilation." Then this verse was revealed. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made expiation, meaning for his oath, and refrained from that.

Ibn Kathir said: This chain is weak, because Salih (one of its narrators) is Ibn Bashir al-Murri, who is weak according to the imams. al-Bukhari said: he is munkar al-hadith (one whose reports are rejected). And 'Abd Allah ibn al-Imam Ahmad related in the Musnad of his father from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: When the day of Uhud came, sixty men of the Ansar were killed and six of the Muhajirun. The Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If we have a day like this against the polytheists, we will certainly mutilate them." Then when the day of the Conquest came, a man said: "Quraysh will not be recognized after today." So a caller proclaimed that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had granted security to black and white alike, except for so-and-so and so-and-so, persons he named. Then the verse was revealed. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "We will be patient and will not punish."

(p-3880) I say: By knowing what we have already presented concerning the meaning of the occasion of revelation (sabab al-nuzul) in the introduction to the commentary, one knows that there is no need to go to the view that it is Madani and was attached to the surah, nor to these reports; for with it the absence of contradiction and the agreement of the reports with the verse becomes clear, so keep it in mind.

The third: Ibn Kathir said: This noble verse has parallels in the Qur'an, for it contains the legislation of justice and the exhortation to excellence, as in His saying: ﴿And the recompense for an evil is an evil like it﴾ [al-Shura: 40], then He said: ﴿but whoever pardons and makes reconciliation, his reward is upon Allah﴾ [al-Shura: 40], and so on. And He said: ﴿and for wounds is retaliation﴾ [al-Ma'ida: 45], then He said: ﴿but whoever forgoes it, it is an expiation for him﴾ [al-Ma'ida: 45]. End of quotation.

Then, Exalted is He emphasized the command to patience, to strengthen steadfastness and endurance for everything one meets in the way of truth, by His saying:

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 16, verses 127–128:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[127–128] ﴿And be patient, and your patience is not but through Allah. And do not grieve over them, and do not be in distress over what they conspire.﴾ ﴿Indeed, Allah is with those who fear Him and those who are doers of good.﴾ [An-Nahl: 128].

﴿And be patient, and your patience is not but through Allah﴾, i.e., by His help and His enabling success. ﴿And do not grieve over them﴾, i.e., over the disbelievers, that is, over their disbelief and their not being guided. ﴿And do not be in distress over what they conspire﴾, i.e., in distress of the chest because of what they plot of the various kinds of schemes.

﴿Indeed, Allah is with those who fear Him and those who are doers of good﴾ [An-Nahl: 128] is a reason for what precedes it. That is: indeed, He, exalted is He, is sufficient for you, your helper, your supporter, and the one who grants you victory over them; because He, exalted is He, is with the God-fearing (al-muttaqin) and the good-doers (al-muhsinin) by aid, victory and support, so He protects them, safeguards them, and makes them prevail over their enemies. Ibn Kathir said: (p-3881) This is a particular companionship, like His saying: ﴿When your Lord inspired the angels, "I am with you, so strengthen those who have believed"﴾ [Al-Anfal: 12], and His saying to Musa and Harun: ﴿Do not fear; indeed, I am with you both; I hear and I see﴾ [Ta-Ha: 46]. As for the general companionship, it is hearing, seeing and knowledge, like His saying: ﴿And He is with you wherever you are﴾ [Al-Hadid: 4], and His saying: ﴿There is no private conversation among three but that He is the fourth of them, nor among five but that He is the sixth, nor less than that nor more but that He is with them wherever they are﴾ [Al-Mujadilah: 7].

Abu al-Su'ud said: The repetition of the relative pronoun (al-ladhina) serves to indicate that each of the two clauses is sufficient for His guardianship, without either being a completion of the other. The first is given as a verbal sentence (fi'liyyah) to indicate occurrence (al-huduth), just as the second is given as a nominal sentence (ismiyyah) to indicate that its content is a firmly established characteristic in them. The placing of taqwa before ihsan is because takhliyah (emptying) precedes tahliyah (adorning). The two relatives may refer either to the category of the God-fearing and the good-doers, into which he, ﷺ, enters at the first level of entry; or to him, ﷺ, and those who follow him. He expressed them by this, praising them and commending them with the two fine attributes. In it there is an allusion that his, ﷺ, conduct entails the emulation of the community of him, as in the saying of one who said to Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, at the condolence for his father al-Abbas:

*Be patient, and we shall be patient through you, for the patience of the subjects is in accordance with the patience of the head.*

And after this verse:

*Your reward after him is better than al-Abbas, and Allah is better for al-Abbas than you.*

Ibn Abbas said: No one consoled me more than this.

And on the authority of Harim ibn Hayyan: when he was asked at the time of death, "Make a bequest." He said: "A bequest is only of wealth, and I have no wealth. But I bequeath to you the final verses of Surat an-Nahl. . . "
